notes: The corridor runs port-starboard, which is west-east in game directions: WEST and IN to the escape pod, EAST to the reactor lobby. The gangway bay opens off the north side of the channel and the sanitation alcove off the south side.

Footprint: the channel is the README's 2.2 m clear width (z -1.1 to 1.1) at its 2.3 m height, with the gangway bay recessed 1.1 m north and the sanitation alcove 1.1 m south, giving the 4.4 m overall depth recorded in `size`. The gangway bay is taller than 2.3 m because the gangway climbs out through the deck head; one `size` cannot say so, and the room builder carries that shape.

DR-087 corrects View A and the README: the routine-duty gangway is open, its emergency bulkhead closes at the base, and the closed pod door reads as a single-leaf slider without a wheel or hinge. Door state geometry remains as authored above.

notes: DR-106 geometry, cut from the one Kalamontee layout (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 95-102, 379-395; scene wwwroot/data/scenes/CONFERENCE-ROOM.json): 6.4 x 3 x 6.4, origin on the floor at the room centre, x east, z south. "A fairly square room, almost filled by a round conference table" (compone.zil 247): the table 3.6 m across centred [0, -, -0.25] on a pedestal, six chairs round it. South: the Conference door, 1.5 x 2.3, the same hole as the Rec Area's north door. North: Booth 1's 1.5 x 2.5 opening, no door. Opening and exit positions sit 0.06 m in from the wall's inner face (z 3.2 and -3.2), the exit panel's half depth, as the Rec Area's -3.94 does for the same hole; on the face would do as well.

The eye is [2.3, 1.6, 1.2], on the free floor south-east of the table: 0.9 m from the east wall, 0.92 m from the table's edge, 1.04 m from the nearest chair (the one at 150; the one at 90 is 1.23 m away). Accepted in the fix pass (Norm, 14 Sep). Not the room centre, which is over the table. Not the layout's first [0, 1.6, 2.25] either: that is inside the door's sweep (1.21 m from the hinge; the leaf is 1.5 m), so the open leaf would stand 0.7 m from the eye across bearings 217-307, and the doorway and the leaf together would span 165 degrees, more than one view can own. From [2.3, 1.2] the two together span 42.8 degrees. The cost: 069 and 159 are close views of the east wall and the south-east corner, and Booth 1's "1" is out of sight.

Norm plan (DR-106 fix pass, 14 Sep): TURN-069/159/252/345, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 133, 1254 square, all from the eye. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 28.95 degrees above and below level at its lowest, so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 23.95) = 132.1, rounded up to 133 (the fix pass's 131 was short; DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep). Seam windows are 112-116, 205-206, 298-299 and 22-32 degrees (spans 90/93/93/84, each under 94). 112-116 is on the east wall, 39.8 degrees from the south-east corner and 101.8 from the nearest opening edge. 205-206 is on the south wall, 11.8 from the door's east jamb and 44.0 from the south-west corner. 298-299 crosses the table's far rim onto the west wall, 9.7 from the north-west corner, 26.3 from the booth's west jamb and 6.4 from the chair at 270: the one seam that cannot keep to plain wall, since the seam between the door's view and the booth's must fall between the open leaf (to 260.6) and the booth's west jamb (325.3), and the table spans 260.8-343.7 from here. 22-32 is on the east wall's north end, 10.4 from the north-east corner and 41.4 from the booth's east jamb. Each opening is whole inside one view: the doorway (217.8-236.8) with the open leaf (to 260.6) in 252, Booth 1's opening (325.3-340.6) in 345. TURN-252 is the base (CONFERENCE-DOOR without OPENBIT) and owns TURN-252@DOOR-OPEN; the DOWN cap, whose south-west corner takes in the doorway's foot, owns TURN-DOWN@DOOR-OPEN; no other view sees the door or the leaf. Fabric renders: reference/DR-106_CONFERENCE-ROOM-{069,159,252,345,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png and reference/DR-106_CONFERENCE-ROOM-{252,DOWN}_FABRIC-DOOR-OPEN.png. The wrap-up (14 Sep) re-made UP and both DOWNs at HFOV 133 and 252 (both states) with the threshold slab, under the same names; 069, 159 and 345 came out byte-identical.

No sky, sun, day phase, flood or power state (ONBIT, compone.zil 239): no view sees sky -- every ray through the doorway ends on the Rec Area's west wall, Booth 1 is roofed, and the UP cap sees only this room's ceiling. Floyd and dropped items are overlays, and no portable object starts here (world.json). The dial is the Rec Area's (compone.zil 260-261): its number and fused face are that room's overlays on the shut leaf (REC-AREA v4). From here its housing shows only on the open leaf, painted with no legible number. Booth 1's ready light (TELEPORTATION-ON, kalamontee.js 148) is a few pixels on its panel from this eye: painted dark, not a state of this room.

Each of the fabric's six chairs is a seat and a back on one 0.08 m square post, 0.42 m high (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 388-393, the fix pass), a stand-in for whatever holds it up. Paint them standing on the floor, on legs or a pedestal base to Greg's taste, under the seats and backs the fabric places.

Engine, not this metadata: the ladder can be extended here (canon refuses only in Storage East and West, Booth 2 and the elevators, compone.zil 668-671; rules/kalamontee.js 279) and cannot then be carried (compone.zil 650-653), but an 8 m ladder has no floor to lie on in this 6.4 m room with its 3.6 m table. The room has no largeObjects.LADDER; where an extended ladder goes in a small room is for the engine to settle (DR-106 fix pass).

Of its six chairs, each a seat and back on one post, the near two (seats 3.35 m ahead, x -1.08 and 1.08) show their inner halves and posts at the mouth's lower corners, and the far two (7.07 m) only their backs over the table top; the two side chairs are out of sight. Beyond the table the Conference Room's plain south wall, its face 8.66 m ahead, seen across 5.7 m of its 6.4 m width (x -2.87 to 2.87: the mouth's far jamb face, 2.26 m out, bounds the cone), and its 3 m ceiling from 3.52 m ahead on (the fabric's two lamps there are placeholders: the Conference Room's own paintings place its fixtures). In the middle of that wall the Conference door's opening, 1.5 x 2.3, centred 8.66 m ahead on the Conference face (bearings 175.05-184.95), the shut leaf in the middle of its 0.16 m mouth at 8.74; visible above the table from about 0.54 m up. Shut (the base): its plain inside face; the dial is on the Rec Area face. Open (TURN-196@DOOR-OPEN): the leaf swung in on its west jamb, lying along x -0.725 from 8.66 to 7.16 m ahead (bearings 184.6-186.0, image right of the doorway), its east face and dial housing ([-0.675, 1.25, 7.36]) toward the eye; through the doorway (its Rec Area face 8.82 m ahead) a narrow slot of the Rec Area: its floor from 13.1 m (the conference table's far edge hides the nearer floor), the east end of its west game table (12.2 m) on the right and the west end of its east table (14.0 m), with the edge of a games box on it, on the left, and its plain south wall 16.82 m ahead. The Rec Area's south mouth and the Plain Hall are out of sight from this eye: the doorway's cone is 2.8 m wide at that wall (x -1.36 to 1.43; the open leaf's east face bounds it on the west) and the mouth starts 2.0 m west of the axis. No people and no loose items in the glimpse; the table bare. The caps (HFOV 133): DOWN reaches 3.68 m ahead along its south edge (23.5 degrees below level), so it takes the mouth's sill and the Conference Room's floor to 3.7 m, with the feet of the two near chairs' posts just inside its south edge, and not the door (its render is identical shut and open); UP does not reach the mouth (its lintel is 66.8 degrees from the zenith, the cap's edge 66.5).

The box is also the floor's pick target here: GROUND has this room's own EXAMINE, SEARCH and LOOK UNDER answer (globals.zil 71-73; rules/connectors.js 166-177), and a floor cannot carry a wall plaque, so the crevice it describes stands in for it (accepted by Norm, the fix pass, 14 Sep).

lighting.notes: Proposal, for Greg to change (README, Look): the Corridor Junction's corridor kit continued -- warm-white fluorescents like the fabric's two lamps (#FFE8C8, at [0, 3.36, -3] and [0, 3.36, 3]; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 793), always on (ONBIT, compone.zil 933), dry dusty surfaces. The fabric's lamps are only there to see by: put the fixtures where the painting wants them and record them here as fixtures once they are painted (a room that authors fixtures replaces the scene's lights). North, down the line, the Admin Corridor's roofless last 2 m, the rift band and the far face across it are lit from the sky over the rift, which this eye never sees: no sky is in sight, so there is no DAY-PHASE state (DESIGN-REVIEW-CONTRACT 6a item 12), and the one base serves every phase. Norm's decision (the fix pass, 14 Sep): paint that region in a phase-neutral dim daylight -- a flat, cool, low grey, with no sun patch and no sky colour -- that reads as neither noon nor night; the lit Admin Corridor North section stays warm inside it. (In the game's day the far face would take the sun: at the Courtyard's sun, bearing 235 and elevation 35 as PLAIN-HALL v7 gives it, nothing shades that south-facing face, as the Admin Corridor's lighting says; its own views carry that in their DAY-PHASE looks. This glimpse, 24 m off through two mouths, does not.) The Corridor Junction, whose north view sees the same face, has no DAY-PHASE either (CORRIDOR-JUNCTION v5).

RIFT-END.beyond: ADMIN-CORRIDOR-N, across the RIFT. The deck ends at the lip 5 m out; the gap is 8 m, lip to lip. Across it the north block's severed face, 0.5 m of broken concrete 4.8 m tall, running on east and west behind this corridor's walls (the end frames x -5.8 to 5.8 of it, 13.25 m out), with Admin Corridor North's whole 4.4 x 3.4 section open in it under that corridor's ceiling: its lit 6 m, the west and east portals seen edge-on 15.2 to 16.8 m out with their signs ("Administraativ Awfisiz", "Plan Ruum") as edge-on slivers and a sliver of the Small Office's and the Plan Room's light through them, and straight ahead, 19 m off, the Transportation Supply's 1.6 x 2.4 portal under its "Tranzportaashun Suplii" sign (fine print at this distance) -- black inside: that room has no light of its own (compone.zil 1195, no ONBIT), and the lamp-light its own paintings show is the player's lamp, which is with the player, here. The grey the fabric gives it is the engine's dark-room rendering (an engine item), not its look. Below the far lip the rift's rock face shows down to about 2.5 m under the lips; the near lip hides everything deeper, so the rift's floor and its sharp rocks are out of sight. Over the corridor's roofless last 2 m the south block's own roof stands on both sides, concrete from the side walls' top (3.4 m) to 4.8 m, running back from the face (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 636-646): it frames the end like the walls below it, and no sky shows beside or over the walls. The sky is the one slot over the corridor's width, bearings 335.5 to 24.5, from the far face's top (13.6 degrees up) to the ceiling's broken edge at z -3 (31 degrees up), less the two tongues hanging from it. The gap is empty in the base; TURN-000@LADDER-ACROSS adds the ladder. No doors. Must agree with Admin Corridor North's own RIFT-END view back across the same gap (ADMIN-CORRIDOR-N.metadata.json).
RIFT-END.notes: The severed end: no wall, no lintel. The side walls stop at z -5 and the deck at the lip; the ceiling and roof slab stop 2 m short, at z -3, with two ragged tongues hanging on (west x -2.28 to -0.52 to z -3.9, east x 1.02 to 2.28 to z -3.6; scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 586-589). "rent apart ... You can see the sky through the severed roof above ... To the north is a gaping rift, at least eight meters across and thirty meters deep" (compone.zil 1014-1017). The width and height are the section, as Admin Corridor North's severed south end (its bay's SOUTH opening, 4.4 x 3.4; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 551). Beside the roofless 2 m the south block keeps its roof, 3.4 to 4.8 m, to the face on both sides (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 636-646), so the end is framed in concrete to the face's full height.

SYSTEMS-MONITORS-DOORWAY.beyond: SYSTEMS-MONITORS, the same 2.4 x 2.8 m doorway (its east), no door. Through it, lamp-lit, the south half of a large room (12 x 3.6 x 10): its south row of equipment tables, three deep, with their boxes of strange equipment, the console along the far wall, and on the far (west) wall 14.5 to 15.2 m off, at bearings 249 to 259, the first three of its seven monitors -- PLANATEREE DEFENS, PLANATEREE KORS KUNTROOL and KUMUUNIKAASHUNZ, left to right -- each with its status strip, red until its system is fixed (the MONITORS states; about 28 x 3 px each in TURN-263); their labels are fine print from here. The fourth monitor (LIIBREREE) is behind the north jamb but for a sliver of its casing and label plate (about 0.1 m, bearings 261.8-262.2, a few pixels; its always-green strip is hidden but for a sub-pixel sliver, at most one blended pixel at the jamb's edge), and the room's south wall closes the view on the left. No sky and no rift: the doorway is under the roof. Derive from the Systems Monitors' own package once it has views facing back.
SYSTEMS-MONITORS-DOORWAY.notes: "A wide doorway, labelled "Sistumz Moniturz," leads west" (compone.zil 1020-1021). No door. The sign is on the lintel face, centre [-2.18, 3.1, 1.5], 1.8 x 0.3 m (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 584); its lettering is exactly "Sistumz Moniturz", 3.4 m from the eye, large enough to read.

ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S-MOUTH.beyond: ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S, the same 3.4 x 2.9 m mouth (its north). One straight line south, all lamp-lit interior, no sky, no doors: Admin Corridor South's 12 m, cracked walls, the jagged crevice across its floor 12.9 to 13.6 m out, and SanFac E's 1.5 x 2.3 opening in its east wall 9.4 to 10.9 m out (bearings 166.8 to 168.6) with a slice of that wash room's dry concrete inside; then its south mouth 17.2 m out, the Corridor Junction (17.3 to 29.3 m; its east and west mouths are behind the jambs, so neither the Long Hall nor the Elevator Lobby is in sight, but the Long Hall's dead walkway, which runs on through the Junction's west mouth to 1.8 m short of this line, shows its flush east end on the Junction's floor just inside the right-hand (west) jamb, 21.8 to 24.8 m out, bearings 184.2 to 185.6, about 4 degrees down -- a thin dark edge a few pixels long in TURN-160; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 472-479), the Junction's south mouth, Mech Corridor North (29.5 to 41.5 m; the Storage East and Physical Plant openings are behind the Junction's south jambs, the Physical Plant's by under a pixel) and the corridor beyond it to where the fabric closes it, 58 m off. Must agree with Admin Corridor South's ADMIN-CORRIDOR-MOUTH view back up the line and the Junction's TURN-013 and TURN-193 (CORRIDOR-JUNCTION v5).
ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S-MOUTH.notes: The same 3.4 x 2.9 m mouth as Admin Corridor South's north and the Junction's four (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 578-579). No door.

NORTH.notes: NORTH PER LADDER-EXIT-F (compone.zil 1001, 1053-1065; rules/connectors.js 65-71): without LADDER-FLAG "The rift is too wide to jump across." and no move; with it the crossing takes 33 time units (C-ELAPSED 33) and lands in ADMIN-CORRIDOR-N. RIFT.label: rift
RIFT.notes: LOCAL-GLOBAL of this room and Admin Corridor North (compone.zil 1004, 1036, 1067-1073). Pick proxy across the middle of the gap, facing the eye, 0.25 to 1.25 m below the lips, where the far rock face shows under the far lip (the near lip hides everything below y -1.28 at this distance); as wide as the corridor's end frames it (bearings -23.7 to 23.7). The rift itself: 8 m lip to lip (z -5 to -13), 31 m deep, rock faces, sharp rocks on its floor (RIFT-F, compone.zil 1093-1094; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 615-629). Its floor is out of sight from the eye.

RUBBLE-PSEUDO.label: rubble
RUBBLE-PSEUDO.notes: "the ground is thick with rubble" (compone.zil 1016; RUBBLE-PSEUDO, globals.zil 2695-2697, rules/connectors.js 551-552). One tag, on the west wall's north pile (the lumps at [-1.75, 0.35, -2.8] and [-1.35, 0.15, -4.3]), whole inside TURN-000. LADDER.notes: The ladder does not start here (LADDER is in STORAGE-WEST, compone.zil 632); the player brings it collapsed, must extend it here (it cannot be carried extended, rules/kalamontee.js 272, 281) and puts it across the rift (SPAN, rules/kalamontee.js 297-299, which sets LADDER-FLAG and NDESCBIT). From then on it is fixed: the port refuses to collapse it while it bridges (rules/kalamontee.js 286-291) and to take it while extended, and ADMIN-CORRIDOR-F moves it to whichever side you are on (compone.zil 1009-1011; rules/connectors.js 120). lighting.notes: A sky room (SHARED-ROOM-METADATA sky.rooms). The same one sun as the Plain Hall and the West Wing, bearing 235, elevation 35; no sun disc. Sky is seen only in TURN-000 (over the rift: the one slot over the corridor's width, bearings 335.5 to 24.5, from the far face's top at 13.6 degrees up to the broken edge at 31, less the tongues) and the UP cap (the strip north of the roof's broken edge at z -3, between the west tongue and the south block's roof on the east); TURN-097, TURN-160, TURN-263 and the DOWN cap see none (checked on the fabric renders). The south block's roof beside the corridor, concrete from the side walls' top to 4.8 m, back from the face (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 636-646), shuts the sky out beside and over the side walls. The roofed south 8 m keep the corridor's own lamp, warm-white, ceiling at [0, 3.36, 2.5] (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 798); interiorLightsOn in every phase. The block's north face and the corridor's north end are in their own shadow at this sun; the north block's south-facing severed face across the rift takes it.

notes: Norm plan (DR-106 fix pass, 14 Sep): TURN-000, TURN-097, TURN-160 and TURN-263, pitch 0, HFOV 120, 1672x941; caps UP and DOWN, bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 128, 1254 square; all from the eye [0, 1.6, 0]. The caps' lens is what scripts/underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (227): the ring reaches 31.25 degrees up and down at its lowest (bearing 211.5; scripts/lib/views.mjs ringReach), and a cap reaching 5 degrees past that needs ceil(2 x (90 - 26.25)) = 128, as the Plain Hall's lens-120 ring has. Fabric renders: reference/DR-106_ADMIN-CORRIDOR-{000,097,160,263,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png, and reference/DR-106_ADMIN-CORRIDOR-000_LADDER-ACROSS_FABRIC.png for the variant. Seam windows (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js solveSeams at lens 120: lo = max(8, span - 52), hi = min(span - 8, 52), spans 97/63/103/97, each under 104): 000-097 at 45-52, 7.8 degrees from the east roof tongue's end (37.2) and 8.75 from where the roof's broken edge meets the east wall (36.25), 21.25 from the north-east wall end (23.75); 097-160 at 108-149, 7.25 from the south-east corner (156.25) and 12.2 from the south mouth's east jamb (161.2); 160-263 at 211-212, 7.25 from the south-west corner (203.75) and 7.17 from the doorway's south jamb (219.17); 263-000 at 308-315, 7.8 from the west tongue's end (322.8) and 8.75 from where the broken edge meets the west wall (323.75), 21.25 from the north-west wall end (336.25) and 45.8 from the doorway's north jamb (262.23). The worst clearance is 7.17 degrees (6.25 in the first pass's ring, with 262). Every window is on plain wall under the roof, with rubble lumps at its foot, fixed fabric painted where the fabric puts them. Each opening is whole inside one view: the severed end (336.25 to 23.75) and the whole broken roof edge with both tongues (322.8 to 37.2) in 000, the south mouth (161.2 to 198.8) in 160, the Systems Monitors doorway (219.2 to 262.2) with its sign and the monitors in 263. The wrap-up (14 Sep) closed the slit under SanFac E's opening in Admin Corridor South with a floor slab (fabric-kalamontee.mjs THRESHOLDS), which this scene also takes: through the south mouth, 16 m off, that slit had shown the renderer's background as an 80-pixel sliver in 160 (x 893-908, y 540-551). 160 is re-made with it under the same name; 000, 000_LADDER-ACROSS, 097, 263, UP and DOWN came out byte-identical.

Why lens 120, as the Plain Hall's -- an accepted exception to the brief's lens 110 (Norm, the fix pass, 14 Sep): between the doorway and the south-west corner there are only 15.4 degrees of plain wall (203.75 to 219.2), so the south-to-west seam is pinned there. At lens 110 that forces the ring to about 348/080/166/257, and then the north-to-east window cannot pass 38 degrees: 348/080 puts it at 33-35, on the east tongue and 1.25 degrees from where the roof's broken edge meets the east wall. audit-turns' proposal, 075/165/255/345 at 110, reads only the openings: two of its windows (28-32 and 208-212) come within 4.25 degrees of the north-east wall end and the south-west corner, and the first also crosses the east tongue. An exhaustive search at 1-degree steps (the first pass's verifier) found no four-view ring at lens 110 that keeps every window 6 degrees clear once the broken edge's corners and the tongue ends count; at lens 120 there are 120 such rings.

The clock: DAY-PHASE, in TURN-000 and UP. Overlays: Floyd, the ladder while it is not across, dropped items. No door is in sight anywhere, and nothing else this eye sees changes.

The base paintings show no portable object, no Floyd and no ladder.

Left to Greg (taste, the fix pass, 14 Sep): how much changes with the monitors -- the three strips are about 28 x 3 px each in TURN-263, and the seven variants stand as Norm's recolours of the base unless Greg drops them; interiorLightsOn in DAY-PHASE; everything in the README's Look. A routine exit, LADDER-EXIT-F (compone.zil 1030, 1053-1065; rules/connectors.js 66-70): across the ladder to ADMIN-CORRIDOR while LADDER-FLAG, else "The rift is too wide to jump across." RIFT-END.beyond: ADMIN-CORRIDOR, across the rift (LADDER-EXIT-F). The corridor stops at a clean-to-ragged lip at the eye's feet 3 m out; the ceiling runs to the lip, with the north block's severed face (concrete, to 4.8 m) above it. Beyond: the rift, 8 m across and open to the sky, its far wall dropping out of sight (the lip hides everything below about 4.3 m down, so the rocks on its floor 31 m down are not seen). Straight across, 11 m from the eye, the south block's severed concrete face, 4.8 m high, fills the width of the view, pierced by the Admin Corridor's whole 4.4 m section. That corridor has no roof over its first 2 m: the south block's own roof (concrete, 3.4 to 4.8 m) stands on both sides of the gap and runs back from the face (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 636-646). At 13 m the corridor's roof resumes, its broken edge concrete to 4.8 m with two hanging concrete tongues reaching out to 12.1 m (west) and 12.4 m (east) (588-589); over that edge a band of sky shows in the top of the slot, under the face's top line. Its ceiling from 13 m; rubble heaped along both walls with the middle clear, the Sistumz Moniturz doorway edge-on on its west wall at 16-19 m (its sign unreadable edge-on), a warm strip light at 18.5 m. Straight down the one line: Admin Corridor South's 3.4 x 2.9 mouth at 21 m, then the Corridor Junction at 33-45 m, where the dead walkway's flush east end lies on the Junction floor against the west jamb of the mouth, a sliver at bearings about 182.5-182.9 lit by the Junction's lamps and the Long Hall's nearest one (472-478); then Mech Corridor North and the Mech Corridor beyond, warm strip lights receding to a dark end about 74 m off. The ladder lies flat across on the axis (LADDER-FLAG, always true while anyone is here: states.LADDER-ACROSS). Sky above the far face and in the slot over the broken roof edge: DAY-PHASE, cool overcast in the base. SanFac E's opening and the Systems Monitors' tables are out of sight.
RIFT-END.notes: Its two edges are the SE and SW corners (bearings 143.75 and 216.25); the whole opening is inside TURN-180.

TRANSPORTATION-SUPPLY-MOUTH.beyond: TRANSPORTATION-SUPPLY: a 5 x 5 m room with no light of its own (no ONBIT, compone.zil 1195; "It is pitch black", verbs.zil 71-73). Only this corridor's spill lights its threshold and the first metre or so of its floor and jambs; past that it is black. No contents, no fixtures painted. The fabric renders show the room lit -- its far wall, walls and floor plainly readable in TURN-000 -- only because of the review page's lighting (this is a sky room, SHARED-ROOM-METADATA v5, and the page lights the whole scene with the sky-room ambient, the Transportation Supply's box included): in canon the room is pitch black. Paint it black past the threshold. (Its own paintings show it lit by the lamp the player carries in there; from here the player is in this corridor and the room is dark. The engine's drawing of dark rooms is filed separately.)

PLAN-ROOM-MOUTH.beyond: PLAN-ROOM: a small lit room, 5 x 4 m (compone.zil 1163-1173). Filling the portal, its far (east) wall of empty cubbyholes: a dark case 3.6 x 2.3 m standing 0.2 m up on a plinth set 0.1 m back from its face and ends (a toe recess; scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 701-708), behind a lattice of 13 upright and 8 level bars, its face about 7 m from the eye. On the side walls only their east ends show, about 0.9 m of each (5.9-6.8 m out): left (north) the Kalamontee Kompleks map with the red "Yuu ar heer" arrow near its top at the east end, just inside the portal's north jamb; right (south) the Lawanda Kompleks map. Both maps too far and too oblique to read: fine print, no legible words. Its ceiling light. Nothing loose.

SMALL-OFFICE-MOUTH.beyond: SMALL-OFFICE: a lit 4.4 x 4.4 m office (compone.zil 1197-1202). The small desk faces the portal about 5 m from the eye, a little left (south) of centre, its chair behind it; the drawer is on the sitter's side, out of sight. In the far (west) wall, 6.8 m off and right (north) of centre, the 1.2 x 2.4 doorway to LARGE-OFFICE, and through it, 7-14 m off: the plush carpet, the front of the wide desk with its chair between it and the window, and a slice about 2.4 m wide of the picture window (sill 0.6, head 3.0), 13.9 m off at bearings 273.4-283.0 between the Small Office's west jambs. Through it ('this installation and the ocean beyond', compone.zil 1263-1265): the plateau's bare rock from under the sill out to its west edge, about 235 m off (273.4-277.5), and its north edge, 235 to 136 m off (277.5-283.0); beyond that a thin band of sea just under the horizon, 0.37 degrees deep at the south jamb and 0.7 at the north (about 4-7 px in TURN-270); and open sky from the horizon to the window head, about 5.7 degrees up. The complex is out of sight: the living quarters and the Long Hall lie at bearing 270.7 and south of it from here, south of the doorway's south jamb (273.4), so the window shows only rock, sea and sky, as the Small Office's and the Plan Room's glimpses of the same window do. Checked on a zoom render from this eye (DR-106 cross-room pass, Norm, 14 Sep): bearing 278.2, horizontal lens 34.8. In the light look the Large Office's sun patch (its lighting.sun, bearing 235, elevation 35, through the picture window) lies on the carpet in this glimpse: the floor 0.70-3.51 m in from the window (measured square to it), 10.4-13.2 m from the eye, over bearings 273.4-283.0 (the whole slice) in TURN-270, with the Large Office desk's shadow in it and the desk hiding part of it; paint it as the Large Office's own painting paints it (ARTWORK-BRIEF 2.6; cast in the DR-106 cross-room pass, 14 Sep). Window sky follows DAY-PHASE; the sea band does not change with the flood (the plateau's edge hides the water line at every level), so it is not a state here.

RIFT.label: rift
RIFT.notes: Pick proxy on the rift's far wall, 0.2 to 4.2 m under the far lip: the dark band between the two lips that the eye sees in TURN-180 (and the south strip of TURN-DOWN). Local global (compone.zil 1036, 1067-1073); RIFT-F: LEAP is death, PUT X IN RIFT loses it, EXAMINE "at least eight meters wide and more than thirty meters deep" (1075-1094). Kept below the floor line so it never reads as a bridge in the graybox, and clear of the SOUTH exit panel.

LADDER.orientation: flat across the rift on the room's axis, north-south: rails at x -0.24 and 0.24, 29 rungs at 0.3 m, 0.3 m onto each lip
constraints: Painted in the base (states.LADDER-ACROSS), in every view that sees it: TURN-180 and TURN-DOWN.
Only its north 0.3 m (z 2.7 to 3.0) is inside this room's box; the rest spans the rift beyond the SOUTH opening.
It lies in the SOUTH lane by nature; no anchor or Floyd spot near it.
LADDER.notes: The LADDER object (compone.zil 632-643), extended "to a length of around eight meters" (680) and spanning the rift (705-707); the room moves it here on entry while LADDER-FLAG (1040-1042; rules/connectors.js 122). Fabric: fabric-kalamontee.mjs 650-657, its parts drawn while LADDER-FLAG == true. It cannot be taken while extended (kalamontee.js 272) and the port refuses to collapse it while it spans (kalamontee.js 284-291, the user's deviation of 2026-09-11), so here it never moves. It is not an objects entry: it starts in STORAGE-WEST (check_design.mjs 189). Engine and review-page items, not the painting's: the engine draws the rules-moved LADDER as a loose box on droppedItems.anchors[0] over this painting, and the review page offers a ladder switch whose false side cannot happen here.

SIGN-WEST.orientation: on the west wall over the Small Office portal, 1.8 x 0.3, facing east
SIGN-WEST.notes: Lettering exactly "Administraativ Awfisiz" (compone.zil 1045-1047), readable from the eye 2.2 m off. Not a game object: no pick proxy. Seen in TURN-270 (and obliquely in TURN-UP).

SIGN-NORTH.orientation: on the north wall over the Transportation Supply portal, 1.8 x 0.3, facing south
SIGN-NORTH.notes: Lettering exactly "Tranzportaashun Suplii" (compone.zil 1045-1047), readable from the eye 3 m off. Not a game object: no pick proxy. Seen in TURN-000.

SIGN-EAST.orientation: on the east wall over the Plan Room portal, 1.8 x 0.3, facing west
SIGN-EAST.notes: Lettering exactly "Plan Ruum" (compone.zil 1045-1047), readable from the eye 2.2 m off. Not a game object: no pick proxy. Seen in TURN-090 (and obliquely in TURN-UP).

constraints: keep all four exit lanes clear (the room's two axes)
keep dropped-item anchors clear
keep off the lip and the ladder
FLOYD.notes: Floyd follows the player here (rules/floyd.js 304-306); the room has no FLOYDBIT (compone.zil 1034), so he never wanders off from it.

droppedItems.notes: Floor points at least 0.8 m off both axes (the four eye-to-exit lanes), at least 1.4 m in from the lip, and clear of Floyd; the room has no furniture.

changes: Painted base, in every view that sees the ladder (TURN-180 and TURN-DOWN): the extended aluminium ladder lying flat across the rift from 0.3 m inside the lip to 0.3 m onto the far lip (largeObjects.LADDER).
LADDER-ACROSS.notes: The base, not a variant. The room is reachable only across the ladder (LADDER-EXIT-F, compone.zil 1053-1065; its other exits lead only to dead-end rooms, 1178-1208), so LADDER-FLAG is true whenever anyone is here, and in the port it stays true (the collapse is refused while it spans, kalamontee.js 284-291). LADDER-FLAG false is never seen from this eye: no painted variant for it. This rests on the port's deviation: were it reverted, the ladder-less rift would be seen by TURN-180 and TURN-DOWN, and both would need a variant. The game text: "To the south is a wide rift, spanned by a metal ladder," (1047-1049).

DAY-PHASE.notes: The clock (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3). The room sees the sky over the rift (TURN-180 above the far face and in the top of the Admin Corridor's slot over its broken roof edge; the south strip of TURN-UP, past the lip) and a slice of it through the Large Office's picture window (TURN-270, through the Small Office's west door). The paintings are the light base, cool overcast; these looks are runtime lighting. Interior lamps stay on in every phase (ONBIT, compone.zil 1034). Light applies before time 5000; crepuscular from 5000 through 6000; dark after 6000. The visual state must agree with g.partOfDay(). The room is on SHARED-ROOM-METADATA.json's sky.rooms since that file's v5 (DR-106 cross-room pass, Norm, 14 Sep), and the six fabric renders were re-made then: 180, 270 and UP show the light look's sky gradient where they showed the interior background, and every view takes the sky-room lighting (the sky's full ambient and the sun key light from lighting.sun, wwwroot/scene/lighting.js 67-104) with the lamps on. The outer rims of TURN-090 (143.75-145) and TURN-270 (215-216.25) also catch the sky over the rift beside the severed end's edges, outside the arcs those views draw (TURN-180 draws it). Engine item, not worked around: as a sky room its whole painting is graded at dusk and night (lighting.js 183-185), the lamp-lit corridor with the sky.

changes: Overlay: Floyd's cutout at actors.FLOYD; never painted.

sun.notes: The Kalamontee sun the West Wing and the Plain Hall use, so the rift and the Admin Corridor across it are lit from one side in every package that sees them. No sun disc in any view.

lighting.notes: Proposal (Greg may change): the interior as the approved Kalamontee corridors -- gray-blue and beige painted steel wall panels, dark deck plate, one or two old warm-white (about 3500K) ceiling strips; the fabric's strip at [0, 3.36, 0] is only there to see by. Daylight from the south end, cool and overcast per regions/KALAMONTEE.md, falling off into the room; the Transportation Supply black beyond its portal. No flicker or damage states.

notes: DR-106 metadata by Norm (the user's decision, 14 Sep), from the one Kalamontee layout (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 544-565 and 600-657, the scene at 976-984; wwwroot/data/scenes/ADMIN-CORRIDOR-N.json). 4.4 x 3.4 x 6 with the eye in the middle, 3 m from the lip. Three 1.6 x 2.4 portals centred on the west, north and east walls with their signs over them; the south wall is gone floor to ceiling. The ceiling runs to the lip. No doors, no furniture, nothing that starts here.

Norm plan (DR-106, fix pass 14 Sep; fabric renders reference/DR-106_ADMIN-CORRIDOR-N-{000,090,180,270,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png, with LADDER-FLAG on, the base): TURN-000/090/180/270, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 131, 1254 square; all from the eye [0, 1.6, 0]. Spans 90/90/90/90, each under the solver's 94. Seam windows (turn.js solveSeams: lo = max(8, span - 47), hi = min(span - 8, 47)): 43-47, 133-137, 223-227 and 313-317, all on plain side wall. The room is 4.4 x 6, so its corners are at 36.25, 143.75, 216.25 and 323.75, not on the diagonals. 43-47 is 6.75 from the NE corner, 20.6 from the Plan Room sign (67.6), 23.0 from its portal (70.0) and 26.2/28.1 from the north sign/portal; 133-137 is 6.75 from the SE corner, which is also the severed end's east edge, and 20.6/23.0 from the Plan Room sign (112.4) and portal (110.0); 223-227 is 6.75 from the SW corner and the severed end's west edge, and 20.6/23.0 from the Small Office sign (247.6) and portal (250.0); 313-317 is 6.75 from the NW corner, 20.6/23.0 from the west sign (292.4) and portal (290.0), and 26.2/28.1 from the north sign (343.2) and portal (345.1). Sign bearings are taken at the boards (x +-2.18, z -2.98). Each opening and its sign is whole inside one view: the north portal (345.1-14.9, sign 343.2-16.8) in 000, the Plan Room portal (70.0-110.0, sign 67.6-112.4) in 090, the whole severed end (143.75-216.25) in 180 with 18.75 to spare each side, the Small Office portal (250.0-290.0, sign 247.6-292.4) in 270. Kept as an accepted exception (Norm, fix pass): the severed end's edges hold its view's seams to 42.25-47 degrees off its centre, which with the NE and NW corners holds the side views to 089.25-090.75 and 269.25-270.75, and the worst clearance is largest (6.75) at exactly 090 and 270; the verifier's exhaustive search found no better four-view ring and nothing valid at lens 120, and audit-turns proposes the same ring. So the 6.75-degree margins at the four corners, two of them the severed end's edges, stand.

Seams on the side walls run 0.64-0.95 m in from the lip (133-137 and 223-227) and 2.05-2.36 m north of the eye (43-47 and 313-317): keep any torn edge of the severed walls within the last 0.5 m, and any fixture off those bands.

Seeds first: TURN-180 (the severed end, the ladder, the rift, the far face and the line south, sky over it) and TURN-000 (the corridor's end: the Transportation Supply portal with its sign, the side walls' north halves, ceiling and lamp). TURN-090 and TURN-270, which carry the Plan Room and the Small/Large Office glimpses, are built from both seeds; the caps after them.

States: LADDER-ACROSS is the base (LADDER-FLAG is always true here), DAY-PHASE is runtime lighting, Floyd and dropped items are overlays. Nothing else the eye sees changes: the Transportation Supply is always dark, the Plan Room and Small Office have no states, the desks' drawers face away, the Systems Monitors' switched lamps are out of sight (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 667-676), and the flood's sea level through the Large Office window moves the horizon line by under a pixel.

ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S-MOUTH.beyond: ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S: straight across the 4.4 m corridor, its solid west wall 7.06 m from the eye (4.62 m past the opening's centre), seen floor to ceiling from 1.99 m north to 1.99 m south of the opening's line (the jambs' outer edges, 2.66 m out, bound the rays); the corridor's floor from the threshold to that wall; and a 0.22 m strip of its ceiling along the top of the opening. Rays cast every 0.05 x 0.1 degrees against wwwroot/data/scenes/SANFAC-E.json and checked against DR-106_SANFAC-E-280_FABRIC.png (the fix pass left this scene's parts unchanged; the wrap-up added only the threshold slab under the opening). Its walls are cracked (compone.zil 923-924). The crevice across its floor is out of sight: its nearest edge, at its bend 0.8 m west of that room's centre line, is 1.04 m south of the nearest visible floor. Also out of sight: both of the corridor's mouths, its lights and everything beyond them, so no Junction, no Admin Corridor and no sky. There is no door, and nothing seen here changes with any state.
ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S-MOUTH.notes: WEST and OUT (compone.zil 1106-1107) share this one doorless opening. It is the same 1.5 x 2.3 m hole as Admin Corridor South's EAST opening, 1 m north of that room's eye (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 116-119 and 459). Admin Corridor South's package gives the same size (ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S metadata, SANFAC-E-MOUTH). The hole's inner face is x -2.5; the position is 0.06 m inside it, as Admin Corridor South's is. The fix pass (14 Sep) ruled the inner face equally fine, so the inset is kept, not required. Threshold: under the opening the two rooms' floors each stop at their own wall face, and the wall's 0.16 m between them was a slit onto the renderer's background (found in the cross-room pass). The layout now closes it with a floor slab in the walls' depth, the opening's width, level with both floors (fabric-kalamontee.mjs THRESHOLDS, the DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep; in this room's, Admin Corridor South's and the Admin Corridor's scenes, not the Corridor Junction's, which keeps its file as cut). TURN-280 and DOWN are re-made with it: the threshold reads as floor. Paint it as floor.

WEST.notes: To ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S (compone.zil 1106); doorless, always open.

OUT.notes: Alias of WEST at the same opening (compone.zil 1107); graybox.js folds it into the WEST panel.

TOILET-PSEUDO.label: fixtures
TOILET-PSEUDO.notes: One tag for FIXTURES and TOILET (compone.zil 1109; globals.zil 2516-2520; rules/kalamontee.js 485-491). EXAMINE gives "The fixtures are all dry and dusty." and FLUSH gives "The water seems to be turned off." The proxy is the south stall's toilet, pan and cistern together (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 517-518: pan [2.2, 0.21, 0], cistern [2.39, 0.7, 0]). It is the one toilet the eye sees whole: due east at bearing 90, between the partitions at z -0.5 and 0.5. The other pans, the basins and the counter belong to the same routine; no fixture is a separate object.

constraints: keep the west lane, the fixtures, the counter and the drops clear
FLOYD.notes: FLOYDBIT (compone.zil 1108) lets Floyd go off exploring from here (compone.zil 2170-2177); it does not decide whether he is here. His spot is floor between the counter's east end (0.65 m away) and the south partition (0.98 m away), at bearing 159 from the eye. It is clear of the fixture proxy (bearing 90) and of the opening (253-287).

droppedItems.notes: The bare floor north of the west lane: every anchor is at least 0.9 m from the lane, 1.4 m from the north partition's front edge (x 1.1, z -1.5) and 0.9 m from the north wall, and more than 2 m from Floyd.

changes: Overlay: Floyd at actors.FLOYD. He is never painted into any view.
FLOYD-PRESENT.notes: FLOYDBIT, compone.zil 1108; he can leave from here, compone.zil 2170-2177.

lighting.notes: Proposal, for Greg to change (README, Look): the SanFac kit's warm-white fluorescents, #FFE2B8, with fill #AAA69C at 0.16 and intensity 12, distance 7, decay 1.8 (SANFAC-A metadata, DR-107). The lamps are always on (ONBIT, compone.zil 1108). No sky or daylight; surfaces dry and matte. The fabric's one centre lamp at [0, 3.16, 0] is only there to see by. Put the fixtures where the painting wants them, and record them here as fixtures once they are painted: a room that authors fixtures replaces the scene's lights.

notes: DR-106 layout: 5 x 3.2 x 5 m with the eye in the middle, cut from the one Kalamontee layout: scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 459 (room), 513-523 (fittings) and 959-966 (scene); wwwroot/data/scenes/SANFAC-E.json. The fabric's concrete is a placeholder; the painted look is the approved SanFac kit (README, Look).

The paintings keep the fixed fittings where the fabric draws them (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 515-522). Three stall partitions stand off the east wall at z -1.5, -0.5 and 0.5, from x 1.1 to 2.5 and 0.15 to 2.05 m high. That makes a north stall (pan at [2.2, 0.21, -2]), a middle stall (pan at z -1) and a south stall (pan at z 0), with cisterns at x 2.39, y 0.7. The wall-hung wash counter runs along the south wall: centre [-0.8, 0.84, 2.22], 2.7 x 0.55 m, top 0.87 m, with basins at x -1.7, -0.8 and 0.1. Above it is the 2.7 x 0.8 m panel at [-0.8, 1.65, 2.49], a mirror in the fabric. The north-west corner stays bare: it is all the Corridor Junction sees of this room (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 509-511).

Bearings from the eye. The north partition's face spans 36-59 and hides the north stall's pan. The middle stall shows only 59-66, behind which its pan is mostly hidden by the middle partition (66-79). The south stall's pan faces the eye at 85-95. The south partition spans 101-114, the counter 164-228 and the panel above it 168-221. The opening spans 253-287, and the corners are at 45, 135, 225 and 315. From Admin Corridor South's eye, the opening shows the east half of this room's north wall, into all three stalls (the south one in part) and the south faces of the north and middle partitions, so that room's glimpse must repeat these stalls.

No painted states. There is no door (compone.zil 1096-1109; world.json SANFAC-E doors []), the lamps are always on (ONBIT, 1108), there is no sky, and nothing seen through the opening changes. Floyd and dropped items are overlays. The base paintings show no portable objects and no Floyd.

Norm plan (DR-106, fabric renders reference/DR-106_SANFAC-E-{008,098,190,280,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-008/098/190/280 at pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN at bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 132, 1254 square, all from the eye. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 29.15 degrees above and below level at its lowest, so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 24.15) = 131.7, rounded up to 132 (the fix pass's 131 was short; DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep). The spans are 90/92/90/88. Seam windows (turn.js solveSeams): 51-55, 143-145, 233-237 and 321-327 degrees. 51-55 crosses the north partition's face (a plain panel below 2.05 m, with the east wall above it), 6.0 degrees from the north-east corner and 4.0 from the partition's joint with the east wall. 143-145 is south wall, 8.0 from the south-east corner and 19.2 from the counter. 233-237 is west wall, 8.0 from the south-west corner, 15.9 from the opening's south edge and 5.1 from the counter's west end. 321-327 is north wall, 6.0 from the north-west corner and 33.9 from the opening's north edge. The opening (252.9-287.1 as this metadata gives it) is whole inside 280. The counter and its panel are whole inside 190. The stall bank is split: 008 draws the north partition's face and 098 everything from 43 on. Accepted exception (Norm, DR-106 fix pass, 14 Sep): the 51-55 window lies on a fitting, 4.0 degrees from the partition's joint with the east wall, and the plan is kept on purpose. The reason: no ring puts every seam window on bare wall. The bare stretches, 6 degrees clear of corners, the opening and the fittings, are 321-30, 120-129, 141-158, 234-247 and 293-309. Every ring of 4, 5 or 6 views at integer bearings was searched at lens 100, 110, 115 and 120, with the windows as turn.js solveSeams computes them, and none fits. Relaxing the fittings' margin to zero (bare stretches 321-36, 114-129, 141-164, 231-247, 293-309) still leaves none. Two long runs of fitting, the stall bank (36-114) and the counter with its panel (164-228), would each need one view with its two seam windows on either side of the run, and no ring gives both. The first pass's verifier found the same for four views by brute force: its best ring by fitting clearance, 007/097/187/280, gains 1 degree but puts every corner at 5. So one seam crosses the flattest fitting, the north partition's plain face with the plain east wall above it, rather than the basins, the panel or the pans. Every corner and opening edge stays 6.0 degrees or more from every window, and the opening, the counter and the panel each lie whole inside one view. The wrap-up (14 Sep) re-made UP and DOWN at HFOV 132 and 280 with the threshold slab, under the same names; 008, 098 and 190 came out byte-identical.

ADMIN-CORRIDOR-DOORWAY.beyond: ADMIN-CORRIDOR, the same 2.4 x 2.8 m doorway (its west), no door. All of it under the Admin Corridor's roof and lit by its one lamp. Straight across the 4.4 m corridor, its plain east wall at x 10.56: 10.56 m from the eye, 4.62 m beyond the opening's centre, seen floor to ceiling (3.4 m) from 2.05 m north to 2.05 m south of the doorway's line (bearings 79-101). The corridor's floor runs from the threshold to that wall. Rubble lies at the foot of the wall: the lump at [10.01, 0.12, -0.3] whole (bearings 86.2-90.2), the north part of the lump at [10.11, 0.25, 1.9] (97.6-101) and a sliver of the small one at [7.56, 0.07, 1.5] against the south jamb. In the Admin Corridor's own coordinates these are [1.65, 0.12, 1.2], [1.75, 0.25, 3.4] and [-0.8, 0.07, 3] (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 593-595). A strip of its ceiling shows along the top of the doorway (the last 1.32 m before the far wall, x 9.24 to 10.56), and the east end of its lamp ([0, 3.36, 2.5] there; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 798, 806) is a sliver at the head of the doorway, bearings 95.6-97.1. Nothing else is in sight. The corridor's two ends, the roof's broken edge (the northmost point seen is 2.45 m short of it), the rift and the sky are all out of sight: every ray through the doorway ends on the corridor's wall, floor, ceiling or rubble (rays every 0.05 x 0.1 degrees against wwwroot/data/scenes/SYSTEMS-MONITORS.json). The layout's fix pass (14 Sep: the dead walkway, the corner fillers at the north face, the south block's roof mass beside the corridor, the Plan Room plinth) left this scene's parts and all eight fabric renders unchanged; the roof mass stands above this room's ceiling and beyond the corridor's walls, out of this eye's sight. The "Sistumz Moniturz" sign is on the corridor's side of the lintel (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 584) and cannot be seen from here. Nothing here changes with any state: the ladder across the rift is out of sight, and the corridor's portable things (the extended ladder on its floor, its dropped items) are its own overlays, never painted here (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.5). This glimpse must agree with the Admin Corridor's own views of that east wall (its TURN-097 and TURN-160; bearings 76-148 from its eye).
ADMIN-CORRIDOR-DOORWAY.notes: EAST and OUT (compone.zil 1118-1119) share this one doorless opening. It is the same 2.4 x 2.8 m hole as the Admin Corridor's WEST doorway, 1.5 m south of that room's eye (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 553, 580-583; ADMIN-CORRIDOR metadata wallOpenings.SYSTEMS-MONITORS-DOORWAY). The hole's inner face is x 6; the position is 0.06 m inside it, as in the Kalamontee corridor packages (the Corridor Junction, Admin Corridor South); the Admin Corridor gives its side of the same hole on the face itself, x -2.2. Either is fine (Norm, the fix pass, 14 Sep): the hole is the same size and in the same place from both rooms. Its edges are at bearings 78.69 and 101.31 from the eye.

EAST.notes: To ADMIN-CORRIDOR (compone.zil 1118); doorless, always open.

OUT.notes: Alias of EAST at the same opening (compone.zil 1119); graybox.js folds it into the EAST panel.

TABLES.label: table
TABLES.notes: "a large room filled with tables full of strange equipment" (compone.zil 1128); TABLES is the room's local global (compone.zil 1121; globals.zil 173-191: LOOK UNDER is the Mess Hall's joke only, PUT ON gets "That would accomplish nothing useful."). One pick box, the middle north table from the floor to its top (x 0.3 to 1.3, z -4 to -1, top 0.75), at bearings 4.3-52.4, whole inside TURN-010 and crossed by no seam. The six tables in the fabric (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 688-694): 1 x 3 m, tops 0.71-0.75 m, end panels at z +/-1.3 from each centre, at x -3, 0.8 and 4.2 and z -2.5 and 2.5, leaving the lane |z| < 1 clear from the doorway to the console. All six are fixed and painted; only this one carries the pick box.

Norm plan (DR-106, confirmed in the fix pass 14 Sep; fabric renders reference/DR-106_SYSTEMS-MONITORS-{270,010,110,130,170,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-270, TURN-010, TURN-110, TURN-130 and TURN-170, pitch 0, HFOV 120, 1672x941; caps UP and DOWN, bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 126, 1254 square; all from the eye [0, 1.6, 0]. An accepted exception to the brief's four views at lens 110 (Norm's decision, the fix pass): the monitor wall and its console run corner to corner, so no ring of four views at lens 110 or 120, and none of five at 110, keeps every seam 6 degrees clear of the corners and the doorway (the reason is set out in the next note but one); one lens, 120, for all five. The caps' lens is what scripts/underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach: the ring reaches 32.05 degrees up and down all the way round, lowest at 60; 2 x (90 - (32.05 - 5)) = 125.9, so 126); the first pass had 131, the value for a four-view ring at 110, and the caps were re-rendered at 126. Seam windows (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js solveSeams at lens 120: lo = max(8, span - 52), hi = min(span - 8, 52); spans 100/100/20/40/100, each under 104). 270-010 at 318-322, on the north wall: 8.19 degrees from the NW corner and 116.7 from the doorway's north edge; it crosses the NW table and its tall unit, and is 5.6 from the console's north end and 10.9 from the PRAJEKT KUNTROOL monitor. 010-110 at 58-62, on the east wall north of the doorway: 7.81 from the NE corner and 16.69 from the doorway's north edge; it crosses the NE table and its control box. 110-130 at 118-122, on the east wall south of the doorway: 7.81 from the SE corner and 16.69 from the doorway's south edge; it crosses the SE table and its control box. 130-170 at 138-162, on the south wall: 8.19 from the SE corner and 36.7 from the doorway's south edge; it crosses the middle south table and its boxes. 170-270 at 218-222, on the south wall: 8.19 from the SW corner and 116.7 from the doorway's south edge; it crosses the SW table and its tall unit, and is 5.6 from the console's south end and 10.9 from the PLANATEREE DEFENS monitor. Every window is on plain wall above the tables; the tables themselves are crossed (see the next note). The fabric lamps' ends stop 0.5 degrees short of the windows at 318, 218 and 138 and 1.5 short of those at 58 and 122 (lighting.notes).

Each opening and the monitor bank are whole inside one view. TURN-270 owns the whole west wall (222 to 318 at the widest): the monitor bank to 37.1 degrees either side of its centre, the switched strips 8.3 to 36.6 left of its centre, and the console. TURN-110 owns the doorway (78.69-101.31, 8.7 to 31.3 left of its centre) and the glimpse of the Admin Corridor. TURN-010 owns the middle north table with both pick boxes, and Floyd. Every seam crosses a table somewhere below the eye: the only table-free bearings on usable wall are 328-4 and 176-212, and five seams cannot all land there.

Why five views at lens 120. The monitor bank and the console fill the west wall from corner to corner, so no seam can land on it, and the seams either side of it must stay 6 degrees clear of the west corners: at 224.2 or less and at 315.8 or more. The west view therefore owns at least 91.6 degrees. That pins its two neighbours about 100 degrees away (lens 120) or 93 degrees away (lens 110). The next seams out then land within 6 degrees of the east corners, or inside the doorway, unless one more view is added. An exhaustive search (every ring at 0.5 or 1 degree steps, with the solver's windows) finds no four-view ring at lens 110 or 120 and no five-view ring at lens 110 with every window on plain wall 6 degrees clear of every corner and doorway edge. Six views at lens 110 do it (e.g. 270/003/022/105/130/177), but only with the west view's two windows 1 degree wide and 6.2 degrees from the west corners. At lens 120 the best five-view rings reach 7.81 degrees; this one also has windows 4 degrees wide or more. TURN-110 and TURN-130 are only 20 degrees apart because the strips of east wall either side of the doorway are 16.5 degrees wide, and at this lens no single view can span from one to the south wall. audit-turns reads only the doorway, so it knows neither the corners nor the monitor bank: its 000/090/180/270 at lens 110 has windows 43-47, 133-137, 223-227 and 313-317, each 3.2 degrees from a corner, and the last two 0.6 from the console's ends.

States. Painted: the base TURN-270 (MONITORS-NONE-FIXED) and its seven monitor variants, TURN-270@MONITORS-DEFENSE, -COURSE, -COMM, -DEFENSE-COURSE, -DEFENSE-COMM, -COURSE-COMM and -ALL-FIXED. Norm builds the variants from the accepted base; they are not painted. The Admin Corridor's west view, the one that holds this doorway (TURN-263: its DR-106 fix pass moved its ring to 000/097/160/263; TURN-262 in its first plan), carries the same eight states, with the same ids and conditions, for its view of the first three monitors through the doorway (ADMIN-CORRIDOR metadata, states MONITORS-*), so the two rooms' strips must agree. Norm plan (DR-106 fix pass, fabric renders reference/DR-106_PLAN-ROOM-{017,110,195,288,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-017/110/195/288, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 133, 1254 square, all from the eye. Spans 93/85/93/89, each under 94. Seam windows (solver margin 8): 017-110 at 63-64 on the lattice's north half (z -1.06 to -1.01), mid-cell between the uprights at 60.0 and 66.6, 14.2 degrees from the case's north edge (its end upright, 48.8); 110-195 at 148-157 on the Lawanda map 0.66-1.06 m in from its east end, 11.8 from that end (136.2); 195-288 at 241-242 on plain west wall, 9.7 from the SW corner (231.3) and 10.3 from the doorway's south jamb (252.3); 288-017 at 330-335 on the Kalamontee map 1.16-1.38 m in from its west end, 19.3 from that end (310.7), 21.3 from the NW corner (308.7) and 54 from the arrow (29.4-33.2). The doorway (252.3-287.7) and its daylight strip (272.0-276.5) are wholly in TURN-288. The caps' 133 is what underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (it reaches 28.95 degrees up and down at its weakest, half-way across a 93-degree span; 131 is an even ring's). Seeds: TURN-017 and TURN-195 (the two maps and their three legends); then 110 and 288 built from both, and the caps from the ring. This replaces the first pass's 015/108/195/288 with caps at 131, whose 015-108 window (61-62) ran a degree beside a lattice upright.

Why three of the four windows cross artwork, and why no ring does better (an accepted exception to the plain-wall rule, Norm's fix pass): the Kalamontee map takes 93.1 degrees of the eye's circle (310.7-43.8), the Lawanda map 93.1 (136.2-229.3) and the cubbyhole case 82.4 (48.8-131.2), with 5 degrees of plain wall between each map and the case. The plain wall a window may use, 6 degrees clear of every corner, jamb, case edge and map end, is only the west wall either side of the doorway: 237.3-246.3 and 293.7-302.7. A view holds a whole map between two such windows only at a lens of 2 x (46.6 + 6 + 8) = 121 or more; the clear positions nearest the case are 6 degrees onto the maps (37.8 and 142.2), 104.4 apart, which needs 121 too. So at lens 110-120 every ring crosses both maps and the lattice. Searched in 1-degree steps: every 4-view ring (lens 110-120) with no window in the doorway or within 6 degrees of an edge has exactly one clean window and one each on the Kalamontee map, the lattice and the Lawanda map; every such 5-view ring (lens 110, 115, 120) has at most two clean windows and still three on artwork, so a fifth view adds a seam and takes no crossing away. Of the 4-view rings at lens 110 this one keeps every window 9.7 degrees or more from every edge and puts the lattice window mid-cell, 2.6 degrees from the nearest upright (the most at 110; more needs lens 118-120 and a 36-degree window across the middle of the Lawanda map). audit-turns proposes 000/090/180/270, reading openings only: its windows sit 4.3 degrees from the NW and SW corners and on both maps' east ends. What makes the three crossings safe to paint: seed 017 and 195 and build 110 and 288 from both (underpaint.mjs), so each artwork seam falls where a built view's rim is its seed's own pixels (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js 334-343, BUILT_MARGIN); keep the legends and the arrow out of the windows.

LADDER-ACROSS.notes: The base, not a variant and not an overlay: the painting must show the ladder, and it never changes while the player is here. The rift is the only way to Admin Corridor North (LADDER-EXIT-F, connectors.js 66-67), the extended ladder cannot be taken (TRYTAKEBIT, kalamontee.js 281) and this port refuses to collapse it while it spans (kalamontee.js 291), so LADDER-FLAG is true whenever anyone is here; LADDER-FLAG false is never seen from this eye, so there is no variant for it. The scene draws the ladder's 31 parts with the when "LADDER-FLAG == true" (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 653-655), and over a whole turn partsForTurn (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js 636-644) drops such a part only when its condition is a clause of a state the views are painted in. So every view of this room is registered with the state "LADDER-FLAG == true" (as the Kitchen's base views all carry theirs, KITCHEN.metadata.json 152-198): the fabric ladder then does not draw over the painted one, and no switch is offered. The same treatment as Admin Corridor North's LADDER-ACROSS.

DAY-PHASE.notes: The clock, for the thin band of sky through the portal (TURN-194 only; no other view sees sky). The band and the daylit Admin Corridor section across the rift are painted in the overcast daylight every Kalamontee view is painted in; dusk and night are the runtime grade. Light applies before time 5000; crepuscular from 5000 through 6000; dark after 6000. The visual state must agree with g.partOfDay(). Interior lights on in every phase: Admin Corridor North's lamps are on at all hours (ONBIT), and the lamp that lights this room is the player's. The room is in SHARED-ROOM-METADATA.json sky.rooms since that file's v5 (DR-106 cross-room pass, Norm, 14 Sep), as contract 6a.12 requires of a room that sees sky. So the grade takes the whole painting down at dusk and night, the lamp-lit room with it (lighting.js 183-185); a level view's sky matte looks for sky reaching the frame's top (parts.js 614-618), which this band, closed in by the portal, does not; and the review page now lights this scene as a sky room (the sky's full ambient and the sun key light, lighting.js 67-104, over the player's lamp), which is not how the room looks: engine matters, not worked around here. Norm's decision (the DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep): the six warm, lamp-lit fabric renders, made before the listing, stay the painting guides, because they show the room as canon has it -- pitch black but for the lamp the player carries (TURN-194 with the interior background where the sky band is; paint the band in the light look). The review page and the runtime currently light and grade this room as a daylit sky room (the sky's ambient and the sun key light over the whole scene, lighting.js 67-104; the dusk and night grade over the whole painting, 183-185). That is an engine item -- lamp-lit dark rooms: a dark room in sky.rooms lit by the player's lamp, not the sky -- so the renders are intentionally not regenerated: a render made now shows the room daylit-grey and the band as sky (the independent review's fresh TURN-194, 14 Sep). Regenerate them once the engine lights lamp-lit dark rooms.

A 0.1 m frame stands round it on the room side (fabric frame part, band 0.1, depth 0.1; parts.js 444-453), so the frame's outer edge is 7.4 x 2.6 and 0.3 m of plain pier is left each side (bearings 231.3-232.9 and 307.1-308.7 from the eye). 'Scratched but unbroken' (compone.zil 1264), 'tough Zynoid plastic' (globals.zil 134): the fabric draws no glass. Not an exit.

WINDOW.label: window
WINDOW.notes: The picture window itself, its whole pane (compone.zil 1263-1264, 1272). LOOK THROUGH WINDOW answers with globals.zil 116-119 (rules/kalamontee.js 48); OPEN: 'This window doesn't open'; MUNG: 'It's made of tough Zynoid plastic' (globals.zil 125-134).

OCEAN.label: ocean
OCEAN.notes: compone.zil 1272; OCEAN-F, globals.zil 167-171. Stands 0.18 m in front of the WINDOW proxy, over the band of sea the window shows just under the horizon from due west to its north edge: from the eye it covers bearings 270-305.6, the band 270-305.8; the rest of the pane stays WINDOW.

LARGE-DESK.label: wide wooden desk
LARGE-DESK.notes: 'In front of the window is a wide wooden desk' (compone.zil 1264-1265); LARGE-DESK, CONTBIT SEARCHBIT NDESCBIT, capacity 20 (1274-1281). Box as the fabric builds it (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 728-736): top 1.1 x 2.6 at y 0.74-0.79, 1.45 m out from the window and 2.95 m from the eye, two pedestals at z +/-1.05, a modesty panel facing the room; its drawers face the window, out of the eye's sight. contentsAt is where an open drawer's contents are drawn: on the desk top, the centre of the engine's 0.3 x 0.25 x 0.3 item box (graybox.js 289-297), later items 0.2 m further east. If the cards get cutouts, set y to 0.79 plus half the cutout's height.

SHUTTLE-CARD.label: shuttle access card
SHUTTLE-CARD.notes: Starts in LARGE-DESK (compone.zil 1240-1241), not loose in the room, so it has no place of its own: while the drawer is open it is drawn with the desk's contents at LARGE-DESK.contentsAt. Once taken it is a loose item (droppedItems).

lighting.notes: Proposal (Greg may change it): the region's one sun, as the Courtyard, Plain Hall, West Wing, Winding Stair, Balcony and Crag have it. From the eye it stands just inside the window's arc (0.7 degrees in from its south edge) but above its head, so no disc is ever in the window; in the light phase it throws the window onto the floor as a patch 0.70 to 3.51 m in from the window, measured square to the wall (the sill at 0.6 and the head at 3.0 m, the sun at 35 degrees up from bearing 235; along the sun's own direction, north-east, that is 0.86 to 4.28 m), with the desk's shadow in it. The patch is also seen through the doorway, so the neighbours' glimpses of this floor carry it (DR-106 cross-room pass): the Small Office's TURN-283, Admin Corridor North's TURN-270 and the Plan Room's TURN-288. The room is lit (ONBIT, compone.zil 1271): the fabric's two warm ceiling strips at [0, 3.36, -2] and [0, 3.36, 2] are only there to see by; the paintings place their own fixtures. Dry, still air; no painted weather.

DAY-PHASE.notes: The clock, not a painting: the shared defaults (SHARED-ROOM-METADATA sky.dayPhaseDefaults), with the interior lights on in every phase because the room is lit (ONBIT, compone.zil 1271), as the Plain Hall has it. Light applies before time 5000; crepuscular from 5000 through 6000; dark after 6000. The visual state must agree with g.partOfDay().
