notes: DR-106 geometry is the layout's (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 557-559, 725-736; scene wwwroot/data/scenes/LARGE-OFFICE.json): 7 x 3.4 x 8 m. The eye is the metadata's (ARTWORK-BRIEF 1.3): 1.5 m east of the middle on the room's east-west centre line, 1.6 m up, 5 m from the window and 2 m from the east wall (the plan note says why). The game: 'This is a large, plush office. The far wall is one large picture window, scratched but unbroken, offering a view of this installation and the ocean beyond. In front of the window is a wide wooden desk. The only exit is east.' (compone.zil 1262-1265). The west wall is the window; the east wall has the one doorway, 0.8 m south of the eye's line; the north and south walls are plain. The desk stands 1.45 m out from the window, centred on the eye's line west, with a chair between them (fabric dressing, not a game object); a 5.2 x 6 m carpet (at [0.3, 0.008, 0]) makes it plush. Walls from the eye: north 308.7-26.6, east 26.6-153.4, south 153.4-231.3, west 231.3-308.7 degrees.

Norm plan (DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep; fabric renders reference/DR-106_LARGE-OFFICE-{002,090,178,270,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-002/090/178/270, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN pitch +90/-90, bearing 0, HFOV 132, 1254 square; all from the eye [1.5, 1.6, 0]. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 29.15 degrees above and below level at its lowest, so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 24.15) = 131.7, rounded up to 132. Spans 88/88/92/92. Seam windows (turn.js solveSeams: lo = max(8, span-47), hi = min(span-8, 47)): 002-090 at 43-49, on the east wall (16.4 degrees from the north-east corner at 26.6, 46.7 from the doorway's north jamb at 95.7); 090-178 at 131-137, on the east wall (6.0 from the doorway's south jamb at 125.0, 16.4 from the south-east corner at 153.4); 178-270 at 223-225, on the south wall (6.3 from the south-west corner at 231.3, 7.9 from the window frame's outer edge at 232.9, 9.3 from the window at 234.3); 270-002 at 315-317, on the north wall (6.3 from the north-west corner at 308.7, 7.9 from the frame at 307.1, 9.3 from the window at 305.8). These are the solver's whole windows, so the 6-degree rule holds wherever it puts each seam. Each opening is whole inside one view: the window (234.3-305.8) in TURN-270 (215-325), 19.3 degrees to spare each side; the doorway (95.7-125.0) in TURN-090 (35-145), its threshold inside the frame too (the east wall's foot is 38.7 degrees down, the frame's edge 38.8). The seam lines cross plain wall and floor only; the drop anchors near 219-224 are overlays. TURN-002 and TURN-178 stop at the west wall's piers (their outer edges, 307 and 233, fall short of the frame's room-side edges at 307.1 and 232.9), so neither sees the window or the sky: TURN-270 owns all of the outside. TURN-178's left edge (123) takes the doorway's south 2 degrees, which TURN-090 owns whole. This ring replaces the fix pass's TURN-000/090/180/270: that ring's 180-270 and 270-000 windows are 223-227 and 313-317, 4.3 degrees from the west corners, and the fix pass cut them to 223-225.3 and 314.7-317 in these notes, which nothing enforces (turn.js solveSeams knows only openings and may put a seam anywhere in the solver's window). Turning the north and south views 2 degrees toward the east wall makes the solver's own windows 223-225 and 315-317 (the independent review's ring, adopted by Norm in the DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep); the 000 and 180 renders are deleted.

Why the eye is not at the middle (the DR-106 fix pass, Norm: the lenses stay inside ARTWORK-BRIEF 1.3's 100-120, one lens for all views preferred). From the middle the window subtends 91.6 degrees and its piers only 3, so no seam can sit on the west wall, and the view that owns the window has to reach 6 degrees past both west corners (318.8 and 221.2) plus the solver's 8-degree margin: 54.8 + 8 degrees each side of 270, a lens of 125.6 at the least. A search of every ring of four or five views at lenses 100-120 from the middle, seams 6 degrees clear of every corner and opening, finds none. Moving the eye east shrinks the west wall's arc: at lens 110 a ring exists from about 1.2 m east, at lens 120 from 0.4 m. At 1.5 m east the ring 002/090/178/270 works at lens 110, every seam window the solver's own and 6.0 degrees or more from every corner and opening edge (the plan note), the doorway and its threshold stay inside TURN-090's frame, and the view is the room seen from its entrance side, as the game has it ('The far wall is one large picture window', compone.zil 1263). No placement moves: the eye is the metadata's, and the fabric is unchanged. The eye move is accepted (Norm, DR-106 wrap-up, 14 Sep): the eye is part of the view plan (ARTWORK-BRIEF 1.3), graybox and the review page honour it (design.js 15), and nothing new comes into sight through the doorway (its southmost ray meets Admin Corridor North's east wall at z +2.6, short of the rift at +3; the independent review). It replaces the first pass's TURN-012/090/168/270 at lenses 110/100/110/130 from the middle. scripts/audit-turns.mjs, which reads the openings only, proposes 010.2/110.4/190.2/270 at lens 120 from this eye; its 190-270 window (218-242) takes in the south-west corner.

States: DAY-PHASE is the clock; DESK-OPEN is an overlay (the drawer faces the window); Floyd, the shuttle card on the open desk and dropped items are overlays. No painted variants: nothing structural that this eye sees changes. The base paintings show the desk shut and bare, no Floyd, nothing portable.

The sea's rise (the Courtyard's SEA-DAYS-6-7 at -10 and SEA-DAY-8-ONWARD at -1, from the base -33) is not a state of this room: from 1.8 m over the plateau every level lies below the plateau's top (-0.2), so the water line is hidden behind the plateau's edges and the band of sea over them is the same at every level. 'Water is visible in every direction' (globals.zil 119) does not change with the day either.

JUNCTION-MOUTH.beyond: CORRIDOR-JUNCTION and the one corridor line north through the admin wing, bearings 344.2-15.8. Cast from the eye against wwwroot/data/scenes/MECH-CORRIDOR-N.json, rays every 0.1 degrees (every ray ends on a surface: no sky); every distance is horizontal from the eye, and to an opening it is to the opening's centre. The Junction (12 x 3.6 x 12, CORRIDOR-JUNCTION v5): its deck, ceiling and the ends of its four lamps, and 18.2 m out its north wall with its north mouth straight ahead (the same 3.4 x 2.9 as this one). Its east and west mouths are out of sight (every ray meets its north wall or floor first), so no Long Hall and no Elevator Lobby. On its floor, left of the axis, the flush east end of the dead walkway (CORRIDOR-JUNCTION pseudos.WALKWAY-PSEUDO; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 464-479), 10.8-14.1 m out, bearings 344.6-352.4, elevation -8.4 to -6.3: it runs on under this mouth's west jamb. Through the Junction's north mouth, Admin Corridor South (4.4 x 3.4 x 12), 18.3-30.3 m out, bearings 354.7-5.3: its deck with the crevice crossing it 21.9-22.6 m out (three dark strips at bearings 354.7-356.2, 359.1-0.5 and 3.0-4.8, elevation -4.1; fabric 487-495; no key, no glint), its side walls edge-on, its ceiling and far lamp (27.3 m), and in its east wall at bearing 5.0-5.1, 25.4-26.2 m out, SanFac E's opening as an edge-on slit: its threshold and the reveal of SanFac E's concrete west wall, nothing of the room. Its north mouth at 30.3 m. Through that, the Admin Corridor (fabric 568-598), 30.5-40.5 m out, bearings 356.9-3.1: only its deck, with worn-concrete rubble along both sides from 30.9 m (the middle clear) and a fallen roof slab at 39.5-40 m, east of the axis. Its side walls, roof and ceiling are out of sight (Admin Corridor South's north mouth holds every ray inside and under them), so the Sistumz Moniturz doorway and its sign are too. The rift's lip at 40.5 m; the rift is only a dark band about 0.4 degrees tall (elevation -2.26 to -1.89), the top of its far rock face under the far lip, none of its depths. Across it, 48.5 m out, the north block's severed concrete face (fabric 607-648), framed by Admin Corridor South's north mouth (bearings 356.9-3.1), up to about 3.6 m at elevation 2.4, never its 4.8 m top; in it Admin Corridor North's 4.4 x 3.4 section, lit (ONBIT, compone.zil 1034), bearings 357.4-2.6: its floor, ceiling and walls, its west and east portals only as their signs and reveals edge-on (bearings 357.6 and 2.4, 51.8-52.1 m out; nothing of the Small Office or the Plan Room), and 54.5 m out its north wall with the "Tranzportaashun Suplii" sign facing the eye (bearings 359.1-0.9, elevation 1.1-1.3; compone.zil 1045-1047) over the 1.6 x 2.4 portal onto the Transportation Supply: through it that room's floor at 57.3 m and its north wall at 59.6 m, dark (no ONBIT, compone.zil 1195; the player's lamp is where the player is, fabric 659-665). The rift band, the Admin Corridor's roofless last 2 m and the far face take the phase-neutral dim daylight of lighting.notes. The ladder across the rift (LADDER-FLAG) is left out: a sliver 40-49 m off (states.LADDER-ACROSS). In TURN-019 this mouth spans x 429-803.
JUNCTION-MOUTH.notes: NORTH (compone.zil 1300). No door. The hole is the Junction's MECH-MOUTH, the same 3.4 x 2.9 (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 106, 122; CORRIDOR-JUNCTION v5 wallOpenings.MECH-MOUTH); check_design compares the two. Its position is on the wall's inner face (z -6), as the layout gives it. The threshold under it, across the two walls' 0.16 m, is a floor slab (fabric 1346): paint it as floor.

STORAGE-EAST-DOORWAY.beyond: STORAGE-EAST: the same 1.2 x 2.25 m opening as that room's west doorway (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 460), 1 m south of the eye, 2.4 m out; no door (world.json doors []). Bearings 100.3-126.0, seen from the north-west, so every ray runs east-south-east, 2.3-7.0 m out: Storage East's deck to its south-east corner, its ceiling and the ceiling lamp (5.0 m out, bearings 100.4-103.0, elevation about 15), its bare south wall (5.4-7.0 m, bearings 115.3-124.1), its east wall (6.5-7.0 m, bearings 100.4-115.2) and against it the shelf unit the Junction's glimpse placed there (a steel unit 0.42 m deep, 2.2 m high and 3 m long along the wall; its face 6.0-6.4 m out, bearings 100.4-112.8, elevation -14.8 to 5.6; fabric 502, kept by the mech wing's layout, 1140-1149, 1320). The room's second, open shelf unit on its north wall is out of sight (every ray through the doorway stays south of the doorway's north jamb). The oil can on its "one dusty shelf" and the cardboard box "on the floor beneath the shelves" (compone.zil 1347-1378) start there and are portable: whichever shelf Storage East's package puts them on, they are not painted into this glimpse, and the engine draws a neighbour's loose things only in that room. In the DOWN cap (right of centre): this doorway's threshold and Storage East's deck to about 1.5 m inside; the UP cap's rim stays above the doorway's head. Nothing seen here changes. In TURN-100 the doorway spans x 838-1121.
STORAGE-EAST-DOORWAY.notes: EAST (compone.zil 1298). No door. Position on the wall's inner face (x 2.2). The threshold under it is a floor slab (fabric 1349): paint it as floor.

MECH-CORRIDOR-MOUTH.beyond: MECH-CORRIDOR and the line on south, bearings 164.2-195.8 (cast as the north mouth; no sky). The Mech Corridor (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1095, 1130; this room's shell exactly, 12.16 m south): its deck, both side walls, its ceiling and its one lamp (14.2 m out, bearings 177.6-182.4, elevation 7; fabric 1186-1188), and 18.2 m out its south wall with its south mouth. In its west wall, bearings 191.4-193.7, 9.4-12.9 m out, a sliver of the Physical Plant through that room's south-east exit (the opening's centre 10.4 m out): the threshold, the reveal of the plant's concrete pier, its concrete floor and its south wall 12.5-12.9 m out -- nothing of its machinery. In its east wall at bearings 170.1-170.8, 12.8-17.4 m out, Reactor Control's door (1.2 x 2.25, centre 13.3 m out) as an edge-on slit: its threshold, the reveal, a strip of Reactor Control's floor and its south wall at 17.4 m; the consoles, the gauges, the elevator door and its button are out of sight, so its REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR state is not this room's. Through the Mech Corridor's south mouth, Mech Corridor South (7 x 3.4 x 8; fabric 1096, 1131), 18.3-26.3 m out, bearings 174.7-185.3: its deck, a strip of its ceiling and 26.3 m out its south wall, with the Machine Shop's 2.4 x 2.8 doorway in it on the axis (centre 26.4 m out, bearings 177.4-182.6); its south-west and south-east doorways to the Tool Room and the Robot Shop are out of sight. Through that doorway, the Machine Shop (fabric 1097, 1132, 1190-1209): its deck from 26.9 m and, 33.7 m out on its rear (south) wall, the chemical dispenser ("Standing against the rear wall is a large dispensing machine with a spout", compone.zil 1640-1644; CHEMICAL-DISPENSER, 1670): the 2.4 x 2.3 body (bearings 178.0-182.0, elevation -2.7 to 1.1), the strip of nine buttons 1.45 m up (33.6 m; bearings 178.3-181.7; their colours and labels, 1654-1659, too small to read at this distance), the spout 0.75 m up and the grate on the floor under it (33.4-33.5 m), and the shop's rear wall either side at 34.5 m. Its corner machines are out of sight. A flask or canteen under the spout (SPOUT-PLACED, compone.zil 1645-1652) is the Machine Shop's loose thing, not painted here. Nothing seen here changes. In TURN-193 this mouth spans x 514-865.
MECH-CORRIDOR-MOUTH.notes: SOUTH (compone.zil 1301). No door. The same 3.4 x 2.9 hole as the Mech Corridor's NORTH (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 122, 1130). Position on the wall's inner face (z 6). The threshold under it is a floor slab (fabric 1348): paint it as floor.

PHYSICAL-PLANT-MOUTH.beyond: PHYSICAL-PLANT: its north-east exit ("exits in the northeast and southeast corners", compone.zil 1434; its NE, 1442), the same 2.4 x 2.8 m hole, 2 m north of the eye, centre 3.0 m out; its north jamb is 0.3 m from the plant's north wall (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 462, 1123-1128). No door. Bearings 290.0-325.5, every ray running west-north-west, 2.4-10.2 m out: the reveal of the plant's concrete east wall and the threshold; its bare concrete floor out to 10.2 m; its concrete north wall, 8 m high, from 4.4 to 10.2 m out over the whole width (bearings 290.0-323.5, elevation -20 to 24, cut off by this opening's head); and overhead the end of the catwalk along the plant's north wall (PHYSICAL-PLANT pseudos.CATWALK-PSEUDO; not its higher east-west catwalk at 6 m), which the Junction's glimpse placed over the doorway's line, 4 m up (its tread seen from below, 4.9-7.6 m out, bearings 290.0-299.2, elevation 17.3-25.5; fabric 504, kept, 1151-1160) -- the catwalks "too high for you to access" (globals.zil 2437-2439). Out of sight: the two big machines, the air handlers and their ducts, the main duct along the north wall (above the opening's head), the boilers, the north-south and upper catwalks, the pump and the one panel with its lamp lit (fabric 1161-1182), and the plant's two roof lamps. "A huge, dim room" (1434): its north wall reads dimmer than this corridor, lit from the plant's own lamps and this corridor's spill. In the DOWN cap's north-west corner: the threshold and the plant's floor to about 2 m inside; in the UP cap's north-west corner, through the opening's head, a strip of the plant's north wall and the underside of the catwalk's end. Nothing seen here changes ("Hardly any of the equipment is still operating", 1437, and none of it is in sight). In TURN-286 the opening spans x 877-1318.
PHYSICAL-PLANT-MOUTH.notes: WEST (compone.zil 1299). No door. Position on the wall's inner face (x -2.2), not 0.06 m inside: the 286|019 seam window is measured from this opening's north jamb (Norm plan, notes), and turn.js takes opening edges at the metadata position, where 0.06 m inside would put the jamb 0.7 degrees nearer the window. The threshold under it is a floor slab (fabric 1350): paint it as floor.

droppedItems.notes: The bare floor south-west of the eye, bearings 205-255, 1.3-2.8 m out: every anchor is 0.9 m or more from the south lane (the line x 0), 1.3 m or more from the west lane (the eye to the Physical Plant's opening, which runs north-west) and further from the north and east lanes, 0.3 m or more from the west wall, 0.56 m or more from each other and 2.9 m or more from Floyd. changes: Overlay: Floyd at actors.FLOYD. Never painted.

Overlay: the ladder as a dropped thing (it starts in STORAGE-WEST, compone.zil 632-643). Neither: the ladder lying across the rift, 40.5-48.8 m up the line, would show in TURN-019 only as a sliver in the rift band about 0.6 degrees wide and 0.3 tall (some 7 x 4 px at about x 634, y 491). The layout leaves it out of this scene, as it leaves it out of the Junction's (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 926, 1371-1375; no LADDER-FLAG switch on this room's review page), and the paintings leave it out: the band is painted the same in every state.
LADDER-ACROSS.notes: Set when the extended ladder is put across the rift (compone.zil 697-707; rules/kalamontee.js 299), and never cleared in the port (kalamontee.js 286-291).

lighting.notes: Proposal, for Greg to change (README, Look): the Junction's corridor kit continued south -- warm-white fluorescent strips like the fabric's two (#FFE8C8, at [0, 3.36, -3] and [0, 3.36, 3]; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 794, 806-807), always on (ONBIT, compone.zil 1302), dry and dusty surfaces. The fabric's lamps are only there to see by: put the fixtures where the painting wants them and record them here once they are painted (a room that authors fixtures replaces the scene's lights). No sky is in sight -- every ray cast from the eye over the whole sphere, every 0.25 degrees, ends on a surface -- so the room is not a sky room, has no DAY-PHASE (DESIGN-REVIEW-CONTRACT 6a item 12) and no sun, and one base serves every phase. Far up the line north, the rift band, the Admin Corridor's roofless last 2 m and the severed face 48.5 m out are lit from the sky over the rift, which this eye never sees: paint them in the phase-neutral dim daylight Admin Corridor South's package set (ADMIN-CORRIDOR-S lighting, Norm's decision in its fix pass) -- flat, cool, low grey, no sun patch, no sky colour -- with Admin Corridor North's lit section warm inside it and the Transportation Supply black. The search: every ring of 4 and of 5 level views, one lens of 100, 105, 107, 108, 110, 112, 115, 118 or 120, bearings on a 1-degree grid, solved exactly (scratch max-min search over every window's clearance to the corners and opening edges): the best clearance any ring reaches is 6.51 degrees (6.36 at the odd lenses), always at this window; a 5th view cannot help (two seams cannot both fit that stretch, and no lens up to 120 lets one view hold the plant opening and the north mouth with 6 degrees each side); 4 views need lens 107 or more to close the ring; and at lens 110 the only 4-view rings with every window 6 or more all have 019 and 286, of which 019/100/193/286 gives the best second window (12.9; 100 and 193 are forced by it). The same ring fits the Mech Corridor, whose openings are in the same places. Each opening is whole inside one view: the north mouth in 019 (34.8 to 3.2 degrees left of centre, x 429-803), Storage East's doorway in 100 (0.3 to 26 right, x 838-1121), the south mouth in 193 (28.8 left to 2.8 right, x 514-865), the plant's opening in 286 (4 to 39.5 right, x 877-1318). No ring does better than 6.51 degrees at its worst window: four views reach it at every even lens from 108 to 120 (6.36 at 115; and at lens 107, which that grid skipped, 018/108/198/288 reaches 6.36 -- Norm's review, 15 Sep; there is no valid four-view ring below 107), five views reach the same 6.51 at 100, 110 and 120 (6.36 at 105 and 115) with one image more. The binding window is always the one on the west wall between the plant exit (325.5) and the north-west corner (339.9), 14.4 degrees of wall: no single view can carry both the plant exit and the north mouth (they span 290.0-15.8, which needs a lens of 118.2 or more for that view's two seams to fall clear of both, and at 120 the next view then cannot clear Reactor Control's doorway), so a seam must fall there, and the solver's reach of 47 degrees past a view puts it there only with the north view at 18.5 or more. At 110 the one integer pair that keeps both ends of that window 6 degrees clear is 286 and 019 (window 332-333); 100 and 193 then give the other three windows the most clearance (the search's best ring). So the north vista's view is turned 19 degrees east of north, and the mouth sits left of its centre. This is inside the rule (6 degrees), not an exception.

Corners in frame: 000 the NE and NW (30.3 each side of centre); 090 the SE (29.7 right), the NE is just outside (59.7 left); 180 none (the south corners are 60.3 each side); 270 the SW (29.7 left).

The search behind the eye (Norm, 15 Sep). At the layout's eye [0, 1.6, 0] every ring of 4 and of 5 level views at whole-degree bearings was tried at lenses 100, 105, 110, 115 and 120, each seam window as solveSeams gives it (margin 8), each window required to lie wholly on plain wall 6 degrees or more from every corner and opening edge and out of every opening. None passes. Best found: four views, lens 110, 1.75 degrees (e.g. 008/100/194/288); lens 100 and 105, no ring clear of the openings at all; 115, none; 120, 0. Five views: lens 100, 3.75 (005/087/117/201/285); 105, 4.25 (008/090/110/199/288); 110, 1.75; 115, 0; 120, 4 (020/045/149/253/276). The reason: the south view needs a window on each side of the Machine Shop doorway on the 12.5-degree stretches of south wall 6 degrees clear of it and of the corners (144.8-157.3 and 202.7-215.2), and a solver window that narrow lies between two views only when they are 81.5 degrees or more apart (the window is 94 - span wide), which puts the south view at 191.8 or more for the first and 168.2 or less for the second; the only other way, two views within 28.5 degrees of each other on one side, spends a view there, and no ring of four or five then leaves the others clear windows round the north mouth. So rather than accept a seam 1.75 to 4.25 degrees from a corner or a jamb, the eye was moved (the note 'Why the eye is off the centre'). At the new eye, audit-turns (which reads only this metadata's openings, not the corners) proposes the same ring, 000/090/180/270 at lens 110.

Seam columns on the walls: 000|090 on the east wall at z -1.26 to -1.75 and 270|000 on the west wall at the same z; 090|180 on the south wall at x 1.87 to 2.14 and 180|270 at x -1.87 to -2.14 (the Machine Shop doorway's jambs are at x 1.2 and -1.2, the corners at 3.5). Keep any fixture, pipe, stencil or panel seam off those bands (Greg's call where the lamps and the wall's own panel joints go).

Seeds first: TURN-000 (the north mouth and the view up the Mech Corridor and the whole line, the north wall's two plain stretches, the NE and NW corners, the side walls' north ends, the ceiling strips) and TURN-180 (the Machine Shop doorway with the dispenser, the press and the lathe beyond, the plain south wall either side), opposite each other. TURN-090 and TURN-270 are built from both (090 overlaps 000 on 35-55 and 180 on 125-145; 270 overlaps 180 on 215-235 and 000 on 305-325); each one's middle -- the side doorway and the shop through it -- is fresh paint in its restore. The caps after the ring.

States. Painted variants: none, so one fabric render per view. No door, no light change (ONBIT: always lit), no sky (so no DAY-PHASE; not a sky room), no rule touches the room (world.json MECH-CORRIDOR-S: action null), and nothing seen through the openings changes: no door stands on any line of sight (Reactor Control's elevator door and the Transportation Supply's portal are out of sight or dark in every state), the dispenser's spout load and the Tool Room's objects are the neighbours' own objects, never drawn from here, and the ladder across the rift is left out of the fabric (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1372-1375). Overlays: Floyd and dropped things. The base paintings show no portable object and no Floyd.

Fabric defect seen from here, for the layout (not this package's to fix): the Machine Shop vat's pipe (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1204) and the Physical Plant's two boiler flues (1165) are pipes written with a `path` in frame coordinates, and shift() moves `at`, `from` and `to` into a scene's frame but not `path` (1446-1450), so in this scene parts 62, 64 and 124 stand 160-177 m east of the room. None of them is in this eye's sight (the vat is behind the Machine Shop doorway's east jamb; the flues are far south-west in the plant, outside its slit), so no render here changes when shift() maps `path`. The Physical Plant's package (metadata note, 15 Sep) reports the same fault.

The east unit is the same SHELVES, painted, but not a pick target.

CARTON.label: cardboard box
CARTON.notes: "On the floor beneath the shelves sits a small cardboard box" (FDESC, compone.zil 1368-1378): on the floor under the north unit's lowest board (its underside at y 0.43), wholly beneath it (z -1.935 to -1.585; the board's front edge is z -1.58), bearing 341 (its ends 332.5 and 346.7), its front face 39-44.5 degrees below level, so it is in the DOWN cap and in no level view (TURN-015's bottom edge is 31-35 degrees down over those bearings). Takeable, open and cannot be closed (flags TAKEBIT CONTBIT SEARCHBIT OPENBIT; CARTON-F, compone.zil 1380-1383; rules/lower.js 210-211, 381), capacity 50. A shallow carton (0.15 m) on purpose: graybox.js draws an open container's contents on its top (graybox.js 293-297: centre 0.13 m over the top, a 0.25 m box, in a row 0.35 m apart eastward), and at this height that row, y 0.155-0.405, stays under the board's underside; a taller box would push its contents through the board. No contentsAt: graybox.js uses a container's contentsAt wherever the container stands, right for a fixed desk or the Kitchen's niche, wrong for a box the player can carry off and put down again. Never painted.

notes: DR-106 layout (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 460 room, 502 east unit, 1140-1149 north unit, 796 lamp, 1349 threshold, 1383 scene, 1406-1409 scene note; scene wwwroot/data/scenes/STORAGE-EAST.json): 4 x 3 x 4 m, the eye at the middle, origin on the floor at the room centre, x east, z south. "A small room for storage. The exit is to the west" (compone.zil 1338). One 1.2 x 2.25 doorway on the west wall, on the eye's axis, onto Mech Corridor North. The east-wall unit is a solid block in the fabric, 0.42 x 2.2 x 3 m, kept from the Corridor Junction's glimpse; the north-wall unit is open, three boards on two uprights, with the floor under its lowest board (0.43 m clear) free for the box. The eye is 1.58 m from both units' faces, clear of everything; nothing moves across the floor (no door).

Norm plan (DR-106, fabric renders reference/DR-106_STORAGE-EAST-{015,106,194,284,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-015/106/194/284, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 132, 1254 square; all from the eye [0, 1.6, 0]. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 29.35 degrees above and below level at its lowest (bearing 60.5, mid-way across the 91-degree spans), so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 24.35) = 131.3, rounded up to 132. Spans 91/88/90/91. Seam windows (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js solveSeams: lo = max(8, span - 47), hi = min(span - 8, 47)): 015-106 at 59-62 on the east unit's face (z -0.95 to -0.84), 12.5 degrees from its north edge (46.5) and 14 from the north-east corner; 106-194 at 147-153 on plain south wall, 12.0 from the south-east corner and 13.5 from the east unit's south edge (133.5); 194-284 at 237-241 on plain west wall, 12.0 from the south-west corner and 12.3 from the doorway's south jamb (253.3); 284-015 at 328-331 across the north unit's front (x -0.99 to -0.88: its three boards and the wall between them), 12.5 from its west end (315.5) and 13.0 from the north-west corner. Every window is 12.0 degrees or more from every corner, opening edge and shelf unit's edge. The doorway (253.3-286.7, and all that shows through it) is whole in TURN-284 (229-339). The frames: 015 sees 320-70 (the north unit from its west upright's inner face to its east end, the north-east corner, the east unit's north end), 106 sees 51-161 (the east unit's face, the south-east corner), 194 sees 139-249 (the south wall and the south-west corner), 284 sees 229-339 (the doorway, the north-west corner and the north unit's west 0.95 m). Seeds: TURN-284 and TURN-106, 178 degrees apart; then 015 and 194 built from both, and the caps from the ring.

Accepted exception (Norm, DR-106, 15 Sep): two seam windows cross shelf units, 59-62 the east unit's plain face and 328-331 the open north unit, because no ring can keep every window on bare wall, and none can keep all but one there. The bare stretches, 6 degrees clear of the corners, the doorway's edges and both units' front edges, are 141-219, 231-247.3 and 292.7-309 only: the north unit fills 315.5-36.2 and the east unit 46.5-133.5, and what lies between them (36.2-46.5) holds the north-east corner. Searched exhaustively: every ring of 4, 5 and 6 views at integer bearings (1-degree steps), at lens 100, 105, 110, 115 and 120, with the windows as solveSeams computes them -- no ring has every window on bare wall, and no four-view ring has only one window off it (a scratch search, Norm, 15 Sep). The reason holds for any number of views: a view's two seam windows lie within 47 degrees of its centre (52 at lens 120), so consecutive windows are at most 94 (104) apart, and from the last bare stretch before the units (309) to the first after them (141) is 192 degrees. One window between them would have to lie 37 degrees or more past north (141 - 104) and 53 or less (309 + 104 - 360): the north unit's usable face ends at 30.2, and the east unit's starts at 52.5 (its edge, 46.5, plus the margin), which leaves a sliver at lens 120 that no ring at integer bearings reaches. So one window goes on each unit: the east unit's is on its flat face, and the north unit's crosses the three boards mid-span, 0.6 m in from its west upright, where the review's straight-line check can hold them level across the join. Of the four-view rings at lens 110 that do this, 015/106/194/284 has the widest clearance (12.0, set by the two south corners). Lens 115 gives at best 9.5 and lens 120 11.3 (036/139/190/293, with uneven spans); 100 and 105 give none. So 110, for all four level views. Moving the eye does not help either (Norm's review, 15 Sep): with the eye anywhere on a 0.2 m grid over x and z -1.2 to 1.2, every ring of 4 and 5 views at integer bearings, lens 110 and 120, the doorway whole in one view, no ring has every window on bare wall 6 degrees clear of the corners, the doorway's edges and both units; so the eye stays at the middle, 1.58 m from both units.

No painted states: no door (world.json STORAGE-EAST doors []), the lamp always on (ONBIT, compone.zil 1344), no sky (every ray through the doorway ends on Mech Corridor North's west wall, its ceiling or its floor, or, through a 0.17-degree slit, the Physical Plant's floor and north wall; the UP cap stops 24 degrees above level, over the doorway's head at 18), and nothing seen through the doorway changes with the game. Floyd, the oil can, the box and its contents, and dropped items are overlays; the base paintings show the shelves bare and dusty, the floor under the north unit empty, and no Floyd. The ladder can be brought here but not extended ("You can't extend the ladder in this tiny space!", compone.zil 668-671; rules/kalamontee.js 279), so it is only ever a loose collapsed item here: no largeObjects.

What must not move, because the neighbours see it. From Mech Corridor North's eye, through the doorway: this room's south-east quarter -- the deck, the east unit's face from z 0.09 to its south end (1.5) at full height, the east wall above and south of it, the south wall east of x 0.07, the ceiling and the east end of the fabric lamp (a scene cast from that eye, 15 Sep). From the Corridor Junction's eye: only the south-west corner by the doorway (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1143, the layout report). So the east unit's envelope (0.42 x 2.2 x 3 m against the east wall, z -1.5 to 1.5), the plain south wall and the ceiling's look are shared with Mech Corridor North's glimpse; paint them there as here. Whether the east unit reads as closed steel shelving or open shelving inside its block is Greg's call, the same in both rooms.

Placement checks (check_design.mjs): the WEST lane is the floor line from the eye to [-2, 0]; Floyd is 1.35 m from it and every drop anchor 0.9 m or more; Floyd is 1.5 m or more from every anchor. The SHELVES proxy (z -2.0 to -1.9) and the WEST exit panel do not meet.

CATWALK-PSEUDO.label: catwalk

lighting.notes: Proposal, for Greg to change (README, Look). "A huge, dim room" (compone.zil 1434), lit at all hours (ONBIT, 1444): dim, not dark, so the paintings show the room in its own weak light, with no lamp of the player's. The fabric's two warm roof lamps at [-4, 7.96, 4] and [4, 7.96, -4] (1.2 x 0.24 m, fabric-kalamontee.mjs 797, 806-807; intensity 14, reach 10 m) are only there to see by: the second is 6.4 m over the eye and 1 m east of it (in the UP cap), and the first is hidden from the eye by the 5 m machine. "Hardly any of the equipment is still operating" (1437): the one panel with a lit lamp is on the west face of the south-east machine (fabric 1181-1182), out of this eye's sight. Through the exits, Mech Corridor North's and the Mech Corridor's warm corridor lamps (on at all hours, ONBIT). No sky and no daylight: no ray from the eye escapes the fabric (the whole sphere cast at 0.25 degrees), so this is not a sky room and takes no DAY-PHASE and no sun. Put the fixtures where the painting wants them, but not across a seam window (see the Norm plan note), and record them here as fixtures once they are painted: a room that authors fixtures replaces the scene's lights.

notes: DR-106 layout (the mech wing, 15 Sep): 16 x 8 x 16 m, concrete walls and floor, placed with the Corridor Junction (frame centre [164.04, 0, 16.66], fabric-kalamontee.mjs 462) and kept: its first exit is Mech Corridor North's west opening, its second, the south-east one, was cut in the fourth pass (1123-1128, 1160). FABRIC DEFECT, for the layout (not this package's to fix): the boilers' two flues are missing from the scene. physicalPlant() writes each flue as a pipe with a `path` in frame coordinates (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1165), and shift() moves `at`, `from` and `to` into the room's frame but not `path` (1446-1450), so in PHYSICAL-PLANT.json parts 11 and 13 stand at x 159.84 and 163.24 -- 160 m east of the room. The layout means one flue rising from each boiler's top to the roof. From this eye only a stub of the flue of the boiler at [-0.8, 2.2, 5.9] (r 0.31, 4.4 to 8 m up) would show: at bearings 201.3-202.7, 16.4-20.7 degrees up, just west of the south-east machine's north-west corner, between the boiler's top and the tread of the north-south catwalk, which hides the rest of it (cast on this scene with the path moved into the room's frame, independent review 15 Sep); in TURN-180 only -- the UP cap's edge there is 22 degrees up. The other flue is hidden by the 5 m machine. The Machine Shop's vat pipe (1204) has the same fault. Once shift() maps `path`, TURN-180 is re-rendered; nothing else in this package changes (the flue is 23.5 degrees or more from every seam window).

Norm plan (DR-106, 15 Sep; fabric renders reference/DR-106_PHYSICAL-PLANT-{087,180,273,354,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-087, TURN-180, TURN-273 and TURN-354, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP and DOWN, bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 133, 1254 square; all from the eye [3, 1.6, -4]. One lens for the ring. The caps' lens is computed as scripts/underpaint.mjs caps computes it (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 28.95 degrees up and down all the way round, lowest at 40.5 (the middle of the 354-087 pair); 2 x (90 - (28.95 - 5)) = 132.1, so 133. Seam windows (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js solveSeams at lens 110: lo = max(8, span - 47), hi = min(span - 8, 47); spans 93/93/81/93): 087|180 at 133-134, on the east wall's plain concrete pier, 15.4 degrees from the SE exit's north jamb (149.4) and 57.6 from the NE exit's south jamb; 180|273 at 226-227, across the flat east face of the 5 m machine, 3.5 m off, floor to above the frame -- 10.4 degrees from the machine's south-east edge (215.6) and 31.7 from its north-east corner (258.7); the room's SW corner (222.5) is behind the machine; 273|354 at 307-320, on the plain north wall, 17.1 from the NW corner, the north catwalk crossing the top of the column at its west end (from 24.8 degrees up at 307) as a near-horizontal line; 354|087 at 40-41, on the plain north wall, 10.3 from the NE corner (51.34) and 12.5 from the NE exit's north jamb (53.5), the north catwalk just above the column's top (30 degrees up there). Each exit is whole inside one view: the NE exit (53.5-75.4) in TURN-087, 33.5 to 11.6 degrees left of its centre; the SE exit (149.4-155.3) in TURN-180, 30.6 to 24.7 left of its centre. No other level view sees either; neither cap reaches them (the DOWN cap's edge is 23.5 degrees down, the exits' thresholds 7.5-17.2 degrees down; the UP cap's is 23.5 up, the exits' heads 5.7-13.0 up). Corners in frame: 087 the NE (35.6 left of centre), 180 the SE (22.6 left), 273 the NW (16.9 right); 354 none.

The one exception, and the search behind it (Norm, 15 Sep). The seam at 226-227 crosses equipment -- the 5 m machine's flat east face -- not bare wall. It cannot be avoided. From the eye the room's south-west half, bearings 158.6 to 289.9, is machinery across the middle of every frame -- the south-east machine (to 21.5-22.9 degrees up, the south wall and the catwalks above it), the boilers, then the 5 m machine and the air handler from the floor to above the frame -- with bare wall only in a 4.2-degree strip of the south wall between the boilers (206.9-211.1), too narrow for a window 6 degrees clear of both, and in the 6.5 degrees of west wall by the NW corner (283.4-289.9), inside that corner's 6 degrees. A seam must fall somewhere in that half, because the bare arcs on either side of it -- the north wall (6 degrees clear: 295.9-45.4) and the pier (81.4-143.4) -- are 152 degrees apart, more than one view can bridge. The exhaustive search: every ring of 4 and of 5 level views at whole-degree bearings, lenses 100, 105, 110, 115 and 120, each seam window as solveSeams gives it, every window kept 6 degrees or more from every vertical edge the seam column sees (room corners, exit jambs, the machines' sides, the boilers, the catwalk hangers; edges found by ray-casting the columns at 0.25 degrees) and out of both exits. Four views at 100 or 105: no ring. Four views at 110, 115 or 120 and five at 105 to 120: at least one window on equipment in every ring, never none. Five at 100: two. The best four-view ring at 110 is this one, every window 10.3 degrees or more from every edge (the best at 115 reaches 9.9, at 120 7.4, with one window on equipment). audit-turns reads only the openings, so it knows neither the machines nor the hidden corner. The seam is easiest if the 5 m machine's east face stays plain where 180 meets 273: its strip from z -2.1 to -1.0 (bearings 220-233), floor to top, with no gauge, pipe or stencil crossing it (Greg's call how, README Look).

Seeds first: TURN-087 (the NE exit and the glimpse of Mech Corridor North, the NE corner, the long east pier, the north catwalk overhead) and TURN-273 (the 5 m machine's east and north faces, the north air handler and its duct, the NW corner, the catwalks overhead), opposite each other. TURN-180 and TURN-354 are built from both (180 overlaps 087 on 125-142 and 273 on 218-235; 354 overlaps 273 on 299-328 and 087 on 32-49); 180's middle -- the SE exit and the view down the Mech Corridor, the south-east machine and the boilers -- is fresh paint in its restore. The caps after them.

States. Painted variants: none. No door, no light change (ONBIT: always lit), no sky (so no DAY-PHASE; not a sky room), the equipment never starts or stops (no rule touches the room: world.json PHYSICAL-PLANT has no action routine; the scenery routines only print), and nothing seen through either exit changes (Reactor Control's door, the only door on the line, is out of sight). Overlays: Floyd and dropped things. No object starts here and the room has no globals (world.json PHYSICAL-PLANT: objects [], globals []); its scenery words are EQUIPM and CATWALK (pseudos). The base paintings show no portable object and no Floyd. No large object: nothing the rules move is painted here.

Out of sight: the chemical dispenser on the shop's rear (south) wall, its nine buttons, its spout and the grate under it (from bearing 128.8 on, south of this doorway's south jamb), so whatever stands under the spout (SPOUT-PLACED, compone.zil 1645-1652) never shows here; the shop's mill and vat (behind the pier) and its lathe; the Robot Shop's torsos, standing half-built robot, charging cabinet, racks of limbs and heap of parts; and Floyd, who starts in the Robot Shop (compone.zil 1838-1843), an overlay there, never painted into a vista (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.5). (FDESC, compone.zil 1534-1535); "a wide mouth and looks large enough to hold one or two liters" (FLASK-F, 1543-1558), so about 0.16 across and 0.24 tall, standing on the floor (centre 0.12 up) under the lowest board (its underside 0.43 up), at the board's front edge. MAGNET.label: curved metal bar

The top board, 2.57 up, would hide anything on it from this eye; on the 1.85 board, 0.27 m above the eye and 0.8 m off, the upper three-quarters of the bar clears the board's front edge. In the bay between the uprights at z 0 and 2.15; bearing 207.9, 1.92 m from the eye, in TURN-175 (and on the left edge of TURN-265).

LASER.label: laser

It has a long, slender barrel and a dial with six settings" (LASER-F, 2657-2662): about 0.45 long along the board, 0.12 wide and 0.16 tall, on the 1.15 m board (its top at 1.17; centre 1.25). lighting.notes: An enclosed room lit by its own ceiling lights (ONBIT, compone.zil 1526): the fabric has two warm-white strips on the room's axis at [0, 3.16, -2.5] and [0, 3.16, 2.5] (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1333, the wing's LIGHTS table), there to see by. From this eye the north one runs across the top of TURN-341 and the top-left corner of TURN-078 and passes 0.7 degrees above the frames' top over the 341|078 seam window; the south one is in the top of TURN-175, 20 degrees clear of the 078|175 window; both are in the UP cap. Proposal, Greg's to change: aged warm-white (about 3500 K) fluorescent fittings, as in the approved Kalamontee interiors, where the fabric has them; if one is moved, keep it out of the seam windows (notes). No sun, no sky, no day phase: no view or cap sees the outside (cast over the whole sphere, notes). Through the doorways, Mech Corridor South's and the Machine Shop's own lamps, and the Robot Shop's beyond. Dry and dusty ("The shelves are pretty dusty", globals.zil 202); no flicker or power state.

notes: DR-106 layout (the mech wing: scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1100, 1125, 1133 the room and its doorways, 1211-1224 its dressing, 1333 its lamps, 1355 and 1357 its thresholds, 1385 and 1415-1418 its scene; wwwroot/data/scenes/TOOL-ROOM.json): 5 x 3.2 x 10 m, x east, z south, the origin on the floor at the room's middle. Both doorways, 1.6 x 2.4, are in the east wall, which is cut once from the NE doorway's north jamb to the E doorway's south jamb with the 3.02 m pier between them put back (1080-1092): NE [2.5, 1.2, -3.9] onto Mech Corridor South, EAST [2.5, 1.2, 0.72] onto the Machine Shop. Openings and exits sit on the east wall's inner face (x 2.5), as the layout gives them. The dressing, all fixed: the open shelving the length of the west wall (globals.SHELVES); a tool cabinet in the north-west corner, 1.6 x 2.0 x 0.6 at [-1.2, 1.0, -4.65] (1219); a steel bench on the south wall, 3 x 0.9 x 0.7 at [0.3, 0.45, 4.6] (1220), with a tool board over it, 3 x 1.2 at [0.3, 1.6, 4.97] (1221); a rack on the pier, 1 m tall and 2.2 m long at [2.47, 1.5, -1.6] (1222). None of it is a game object: SHELVES is the only thing here the game names that is not portable, and there are no scenery words (world.json TOOL-ROOM pseudo []).

The eye is [-1.2, 1.6, -0.4]: 1.2 m west and 0.4 m north of the room's middle, 0.8 m from the shelving's front, 3.95 m from the tool cabinet's front and 4.65 m from the bench's; in no furniture, and there is no door to sweep. Moved from the layout's [0, 1.6, 0] for the view plan, and only for it (Norm, the DR-106 metadata pass, 15 Sep). From the middle no ring meets the brief: the east wall holds both doorways (28.0-38.9 and 88.2-121.3 from the middle) with the pier rack between them (42.2-78.7), the north-east corner is 1.4 degrees from the NE doorway, and the west wall is shelving from corner to corner on five uprights 2.15 m apart. Searched with scratch tools (1-degree bearings; lens 100-120 in 1-degree steps; the solver's margin 8, wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js 379-387; no window may touch an opening; a window's clearance is to every corner, jamb, fixture end and upright, and to a ceiling lamp's ends where the lamp lies inside either frame there, a window under such a lamp counting as a crossing). From the middle: no ring of 4 or 5 views keeps every window 6 degrees from every edge (the best 4-view ring at 4 degrees, 010/100/190/280 at lens 107, crosses the pier rack and two bays of shelving and comes 4.2 from an upright). Then over the floor (286 eyes: a 0.3 m grid, x -1.5 to 1.2, z -3.6 to 3.2, and 0.1 m around the best): no eye has a 4-view ring with every window on plain wall; none has one with a single window off plain wall that keeps 6 degrees (the best is 4.5: plain wall is only on the north and east walls, and from most of the floor the north lamp hangs over the north wall's clear stretch); eyes south-west of the middle ([-0.9, 1.6, 1.6] to [-1.2, 1.6, 1.8]) reach 7.0-7.3 with one window on the shelving and one under the north lamp, and eyes south-east of it ([0.6, 1.6, 1.6] to [1.2, 1.6, 1.6]) 7.5-8.1 with one on the shelving and one on the tool board; eyes west of it ([-1.1, 1.6, -0.3] to [-1.5, 1.6, -0.5]) reach 7.2-9.7 with two windows on the shelving's boards, mid-bay, and none under a lamp, on a fixture or on an upright. Of those, [-1.2, 1.6, -0.4] (8.6) is the best that keeps the boards 0.8 m off; [-1.3, 1.6, -0.4] reaches 9.7 at 0.7 m from them. Five views never do better at this eye (a fifth adds a window on the pier rack). The cost: TURN-265 looks at the shelving from 0.8 m, and the doorways are seen at more of a slant (the NE doorway 13.2 degrees wide, the E one 22.5), so the end hall's lamp and the Mech Corridor, which the middle sees through the NE doorway, are out of sight (the beyond lines).

Norm plan (the DR-106 metadata pass, 15 Sep; fabric renders reference/DR-106_TOOL-ROOM-{078,175,265,341,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-078/175/265/341, pitch 0, HFOV 114, 1672x941; caps UP and DOWN at bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 131, 1254 square; all from the eye [-1.2, 1.6, -0.4]. One lens for the ring. The caps' 131 is what underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (scripts/lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 29.85 degrees up and down at its weakest (bearing 29.5), so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 24.85) = 130.3, rounded up. Spans 97/90/76/97, each under the solver's 98 at this lens (turn.js solveSeams: lo = max(8, span - 49), hi = min(span - 8, 49)). Seam windows: 078|175 at 126-127, plain east wall 0.8-0.9 m south of the E doorway (z 2.3-2.4), 8.6 degrees from that doorway's south jamb (117.4), 18.6 from the SE corner (145.6) and 20.2 from the bench (147.2); 175|265 at 216-224, across the shelving's boards in the bay between the uprights at z 0 and 2.15 (the boards' front edge at z 0.43-0.70, their back at 0.95-1.39), 8.8 from the upright at z 2.15 (207.2) and 18.0 from the one at z 0 (242.0); 265|341 at 292-314, across the boards in the bay between the uprights at z -2.15 and 0 (front edge at z -0.72 to -1.17, back -0.93 to -1.66), 9.0 from the upright at z -2.15 (323.0) and 38 from the one at z 0 (253.9); 341|078 at 29-30, plain north wall 1.35-1.46 m east of the room's axis, 8.8 from the NE corner (38.8), 10.7 from the NE doorway's north jamb (40.7) and 17.6 from the tool cabinet (11.4), the north ceiling lamp's far edge 0.7 degrees above the frames' top there. Both doorways are whole inside TURN-078: the NE doorway (40.7-53.9) and the E doorway (94.9-117.4), with the pier rack (57.8-88.4) between them. The accepted exception, after the search in the note above: two of the four windows cross the shelving's boards, mid-bay, 8.8 degrees or more from every upright. What makes them safe to paint is the order of work (next note). audit-turns, which reads the openings only, proposes 047/106/207/307 at lens 120, a view on each doorway: from this eye its windows lie across the pier rack and into the E doorway's arc (55-98), on the bench and tool board under the south lamp (155-158), 1.1 degrees from the upright at z 0 (255-259) and on the tool cabinet (355-359).

Seeds first: TURN-078 (the east wall: both doorways and everything through them, the pier with its rack, the north-east corner and the east end of the north wall) and TURN-265 (the shelving, from the bay south of the eye to the bay north of it, and the floor in front of it). TURN-175 (the south wall with the bench and its tool board, the south-west corner, the shelving's south end and the east wall's south end) and TURN-341 (the north wall with the tool cabinet, the north-west corner and the shelving's north end) are built from both seeds: 175 overlaps 078 over 118-135 and 265 over 208-232; 341 overlaps 265 over 284-322 and 078 over 21-38. Both shelving windows (216-224 and 292-314) then fall where a built view's rim is 265's own pixels, and both plain-wall windows where it is 078's (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js 334-343, BUILT_MARGIN). The caps last, from the ring.

No painted variants: no door, no structural state, and no rule for this room (world.json TOOL-ROOM action null; nothing in wwwroot/rules/*.js names it). Floyd, the four things that start here (and the battery in the laser), the ladder and dropped things are overlays; the base paintings show the room empty and at rest: the shelves bare but for their dust, nothing on the bench. Nothing seen through the doorways changes: Mech Corridor South and the Machine Shop have no structural state in sight (the dispenser and whatever stands under its spout are out of sight), and the Robot Shop's Floyd is an overlay of that room. No sky, sun, day phase, flood or power state: every ray from the eye over the whole sphere (0.25 x 0.5 degrees) ends on a surface of this room or of the rooms beyond (none escapes to the background), and the room is ONBIT (compone.zil 1526). So it is not a sky room and is not listed in SHARED-ROOM-METADATA sky.rooms.

MECH-CORRIDOR-S-MOUTH.beyond: MECH-CORRIDOR-S: its south doorway, the same 2.4 x 2.8 m opening seen from its side (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1131-1132); no door, and the two rooms' walls make one reveal 0.16 m deep with a threshold slab under it (1354). 3.6 m from the eye to its centre, over bearings 341.6-18.4. Measured on the fabric (scenes/MACHINE-SHOP.json, cast from this eye; DR-106_MACHINE-SHOP-342_FABRIC.png), every distance from the eye. Mech Corridor South ("The corridor ends here with doorways to the southwest, south, and southeast", compone.zil 1323): its deck from the threshold (3.7 m) to 12.2 m, its ceiling with its two lamps on the axis at 5.7 and 9.7 m (fabric 1331), the north ends of its side walls along this doorway's edges (11.5-12.3 m) and its north wall, 11.8 m off, round the 3.4 x 2.9 mouth onto the Mech Corridor (fabric 1131). Its south-west and south-east doorways are in its side walls 4.5-6.1 m out, beyond this doorway's reach. Through the mouth, the one corridor line north as a narrowing run of lit halls: the Mech Corridor (compone.zil 1304-1317), 11.9-24.0 m, its walls from 15.6 m -- in its east wall at bearings 7.2-7.7, 16.7-17.9 m off, a dark slit about 3 px wide of Reactor Control's 1.2 x 2.25 m door (its reveal only: a ray from here meets that doorway at 7.4 degrees and would need 1.23 m of its 1.2 m width to cross the two walls' 0.16 m, so the room beyond is out of sight and not in this scene), and in its west wall at 353.3-354.0, 19.1-21.5 m off, the Physical Plant's south-east exit: a sliver of the plant's concrete floor and of its north wall 33.8 m off (fabric 1124, 1128); Mech Corridor North (compone.zil 1289-1302), 24.1-36.1 m, its lamp at 33 m; the Corridor Junction (888), 36.3-48.3 m, its floor and the wall round its north mouth; Admin Corridor South (919), 48.4-60.4 m, the crevice across its floor at 52 m (fabric 487-493); the Admin Corridor (993), 60.6-70.6 m, the rubble along its floor (fabric 591); the rift, 70.6-78.6 m, a line one or two pixels high where Admin Corridor North's severed floor edge faces this way; Admin Corridor North (1023), 78.6-84.6 m, and on its north wall, 84.5 m off, the "Tranzportaashun Suplii" sign (compone.zil 1045-1047; fabric 603) over its north portal; through the portal, dark, the Transportation Supply (1182; no ONBIT): its back wall at 89.7 m, black from here -- it is lamp-lit only in its own paintings. No sky: a ray through the line never rises above Admin Corridor North's ceiling past the rift (the Admin Corridor's roofless last 2 m, 68.6-70.6 m off, needs 1.49 degrees up; Admin Corridor South's north mouth, its head 2.9 m at 60.4 m, lets through 1.23), as the Junction sees none (fabric 540-543). The ladder across the rift (LADDER-FLAG, compone.zil 1040-1042, 1048-1049) is left out, as from every eye on this line (fabric 1372-1375): a sliver 70-79 m off, no switch (states.LADDER-ACROSS-RIFT). In the UP and DOWN caps: nothing of it (the DOWN cap's edge stops 1 degree short of the threshold). Nothing else seen here changes with the game. Derive from Mech Corridor South's, the Mech Corridor's and the admin line's own packages once they have art; no Floyd, no loose items (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.5).

TOOL-ROOM-MOUTH.beyond: TOOL-ROOM: its east doorway ("Exits lead northeast and east", compone.zil 1519), the same 1.6 x 2.4 m opening seen from its side, 0.72 m south of the Tool Room's middle and 1.12 m south of its eye [-1.2, 1.6, -0.4] (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1100, 1125, 1132); no door, one reveal 0.16 m deep with a threshold slab under it (1357). 3.51 m from the eye to its centre, over bearings 260.9-286.5. Measured on the fabric (scenes/MACHINE-SHOP.json, cast from this eye; DR-106_MACHINE-SHOP-252_FABRIC.png), every distance from the eye: the Tool Room's deck from the threshold (3.7 m) to 8.9 m and its ceiling from 7.4 m; straight across, 8.2-9.0 m off, the open shelving the length of its west wall ("apparently a storage room for tools", 1519; SHELVES is a global there, 1527): four bare boards at 0.45, 1.15, 1.85 and 2.55 m up and two of its uprights, at bearings 261.6-262.3 and 276.2-276.8 (fabric 1217-1218), with the plain west wall behind them at 8.7-9.0 m; along the doorway's north jamb, the reveal of the pier between the Tool Room's two doorways (285.9-286.5; fabric 1216). Out of sight: its tool cabinet in the north-west corner, its bench and tool board on the south wall, the rack on the pier, and its two lamps. The flask "on the floor below the lowest shelf" and the magnet "on an upper shelf" (compone.zil 1535, 1564) are that room's portable things, its overlays: never painted here. Nothing seen here changes with the game. Derive from the Tool Room's own package once it has art; no Floyd, no loose items (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.5).

ROBOT-SHOP-MOUTH.beyond: ROBOT-SHOP: its west doorway ("This room, with exits west and northwest", compone.zil 1826), the same 1.6 x 2.4 m opening seen from its side, 0.72 m south of the Robot Shop's eye (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1101, 1126, 1132); no door, one reveal 0.16 m deep with a threshold slab under it (1358). 3.51 m from the eye to its centre, over bearings 73.5-99.1. Measured on the fabric (scenes/MACHINE-SHOP.json, cast from this eye; DR-106_MACHINE-SHOP-072_FABRIC.png), every distance from the eye: the Robot Shop's deck from the threshold (3.7 m) to 10.7 m and its ceiling from 9.2 m, with the end of one of its lamps at the doorway's top right (97.9-98.6; fabric 1334); across the whole doorway, 10.6-11.4 m off, the bench along its east wall (fabric 1234) and on it, left to right, a boxy torso (74.2-76.5, 11.1-11.6 m; 1235), a round torso (86.4-88.9, 10.8-11.0 m; 1236) and a head (95.4-97.3, 11.0-11.3 m; 1237) -- "robot-like devices of every conceivable description, all in various states of disassembly" (compone.zil 1826-1828); low by the south jamb, 6.8-7.4 m off, the robot on its back (97.1-98.6; fabric 1241); behind the bench its east wall, 11.7-12.1 m. Along the north jamb, the reveal of the pier between the Robot Shop's two doorways (73.9-74.1; fabric 1233). Out of sight: the half-built robot standing in its north-east (bearing about 64 from here), the racks of limbs on its south wall, the heap of parts in its south-west corner and the charging cabinet on its north wall. Floyd starts in the Robot Shop (compone.zil 1838-1843) and the layout keeps the open floor west of its eye for him (fabric 1229-1231), which this glimpse crosses: he is drawn only in the room he is in (sceneObjects), so never here, and never painted (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.3, 3.5). Nothing seen here changes with the game. Derive from the Robot Shop's own package once it has art; no Floyd, no loose items.

NORTH.notes: "Doorways lead north, east, and west" (compone.zil 1641; NORTH TO MECH-CORRIDOR-S, 1630), on the axis; it matches Mech Corridor South's 2.4 x 2.8 m south doorway (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1131).

EAST.notes: EAST TO ROBOT-SHOP (compone.zil 1631), 0.64 m north of the middle, where it meets the Robot Shop's 1.6 x 2.4 m west doorway (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1101, 1126). From the eye it is 0.24 m north of abeam.

WEST.notes: WEST TO TOOL-ROOM (compone.zil 1632), 0.64 m north of the middle, where it meets the Tool Room's 1.6 x 2.4 m east doorway (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1100, 1125). From the eye it is 0.24 m north of abeam.

CHEMICAL-DISPENSER.label: chemical dispenser
CHEMICAL-DISPENSER.notes: Fixed (flags MUNGBIT NDESCBIT, no TAKEBIT; compone.zil 1670-1676), so its anchor never lapses. "Standing against the rear wall is a large dispensing machine with a spout" (1643-1644): the fabric's body on the south wall on the axis, x -1.2 to 1.2, 0-2.3 m up, its face at z 3.2 (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1197); on the face the strip of nine buttons at 1.45 m (1198-1199), the spout 0.75 m up, standing 0.25 m out of the face (1200), and on the floor under it a 0.6 x 0.45 m grate (1201). What is put under the spout (CHEMICAL-DISPENSER-F, compone.zil 1680-1690; rules/lower.js 123-129; CHEM-SPOUT-PSEUDO, globals.zil 2680-2689) is moved into the room, not into the dispenser, and the global SPOUT-PLACED names it, so contentsAt does not apply: its spot is the grate, [0, 0.02 + half its height, 2.95] (states.THING-UNDER-SPOUT). MACHIN is one of the dispenser's synonyms (compone.zil 1673), so "machine" means the dispenser; the mill, vat, lathe and press are dressing, not pick targets.

RED-BUTTON.label: red button
RED-BUTTON.notes: KUULINTS 1: the first of the nine, left to right as the player faces the dispenser (compone.zil 1653-1659), so the east end of the strip. compone.zil 1692-1699, C-MOVE 1 ("red" fluid, COLOR-LTBL 1775-1785); CHEM-BUTTON-F 1787-1820, rules/lower.js 92-117. Fixed (NDESCBIT, no TAKEBIT). The fabric's nine 0.1 m buttons are 0.2 m apart at x -0.8 to 0.8 (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1199); the metadata's order wins over the fabric's placeholder colours, which group them from the west end (notes).

SQUARE-WHITE-BUTTON.label: square white button
SQUARE-WHITE-BUTTON.notes: "One of these is square and says BAAS" (compone.zil 1657-1658; object 1764-1771, C-MOVE 9, clear fluid). The eighth of the nine. It also answers to BAAS and BASE (rules/lower.js 429-431, the user's decision of 11 Sep). Fixed.

ROUND-WHITE-BUTTON.label: round white button
ROUND-WHITE-BUTTON.notes: "The other white button is round and says ASID" (compone.zil 1658-1659; object 1755-1762, C-MOVE 8, clear fluid). The last of the nine, the west end of the strip. It also answers to ASID and ACID (rules/lower.js 429-430). Fixed.

CHEM-SPOUT-PSEUDO.label: spout
CHEM-SPOUT-PSEUDO.notes: The word SPOUT (compone.zil 1634; globals.zil 2680-2689; rules/lower.js 360-365): PUT X UNDER SPOUT is PUT X UNDER the dispenser, LOOK UNDER SPOUT names what sits there. The fabric's spout (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1200), 0.1 x 0.25 m standing 0.25 m out of the dispenser's face at 0.75 m, the proxy 0.04 m wider to be clickable. Below the button strip (1.45 m), so the two never meet.

changes: Overlay: the thing put under the spout -- the flask or the canteen (the two the click menu offers, rules/lower.js 389), or anything typed -- standing on the grate at [0, 0.02 + half its height, 2.95], its foot on the grate and its mouth under the spout; never painted. "Sitting under the spout is a ..." (compone.zil 1645-1652). The flask's fill (CHEMICAL-FLUID in FLASK, "milky white", compone.zil 1798-1803) is the flask's own overlay.
THING-UNDER-SPOUT.notes: CHEMICAL-DISPENSER-F moves the thing into the room and sets SPOUT-PLACED to it (compone.zil 1680-1690; rules/lower.js 126). It starts GROUND (misc.zil 83; rules/lower.js 496); taking the thing frees the spout (verbs.zil 584-585; engine/verbs.js 323), and so does dissolving or burning it (rules/lower.js 175, 292). Engine item, not this metadata's to settle: graybox draws a thing in the room on the drop anchors, and nothing yet puts the SPOUT-PLACED object on the grate, as contentsAt puts the canteen in the Kitchen dispenser's niche (wwwroot/scene/design.js 68-73). The spot is given here for when it does.

changes: Overlay: a restrained damaged finish on the dispenser's face, as the Kitchen's DISPENSER-DAMAGED is (KITCHEN v17); no break in the fixed body, and never painted. It lies wholly inside TURN-162 (the dispenser, 161.6-198.4).
DISPENSER-DAMAGED.notes: Pouring the acid or base fluid (CHEMICAL-FLAG 8 or 9, from the two white buttons) on the dispenser, which is MUNGBIT: "The chemical dispenser seems to undergo some damage as a result of your action" (compone.zil 3083-3088; rules/lower.js 191-193). After that every button only "coughs a few times, but nothing else happens" (compone.zil 1789-1791; rules/lower.js 95).

changes: Neither: the ladder laid across the rift (compone.zil 1040-1042, 1048-1049), 70-79 m up the line through the north doorway, is left out of this scene as it is from every eye on the line (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1372-1375): a sliver under a pixel's height from here. The paintings are right with it or without it.

lighting.notes: An enclosed workshop lit by its own ceiling fluorescents: the fabric has four warm-white strips at [+-1.75, 3.56, +-2] (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1332), there only to see by; the fittings and their places are the painter's. ONBIT (compone.zil 1633): always lit, no power or flicker state. No daylight and no sky anywhere in sight (see MECH-CORRIDOR-S-MOUTH.beyond); the three doorways show their own rooms' lamplight, and the line north runs down to the black of the Transportation Supply's portal. Dry and dusty; the fluid that pours from the spout "spills onto the floor, and dries up" (compone.zil 1795-1796, 1811-1812), so no puddles or stains.

constraints: keep the three doorway lanes and the walk from the north doorway to the dispenser (|x| under 1.2) clear
keep the lathe (x -3.3 to -2.5), the dispenser and the dropped-item anchors clear
FLOYD.notes: FLOYDBIT (compone.zil 1633): Floyd follows the player here and may go exploring from here (rules/floyd.js 296); with nothing under the spout he sometimes pushes a button and giggles as the fluid splashes (MACHINE-SHOP-F M-END, compone.zil 1660-1668; rules/lower.js 72-79), a moment of text, not a pose. His spot is at the dispenser's west end, between it and the lathe: 0.7 m from the lathe, 1.4 m from the dispenser's corner, 2.4 m from the west lane, 2.9 m from the eye at bearing 218 (TURN-252).

droppedItems.notes: The open floor south-east of the eye, between the walk to the dispenser (|x| under 1.2) and the press (x 1.9 to 3.3, z 1.7 to 3.1): 0.79 m or more from the east lane, 1.46 m or more from the north lane's end at the eye, 0.54 m or more from the press, 3.1 m or more from Floyd. Bearings 123-144 from the eye, 1.5-2.5 m off: at the foot of TURN-162 and in the DOWN cap.

notes: DR-106 layout (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1097, 1132, machineShop() 1190-1209, lamps 1332, thresholds 1357-1358, scene 1382, scene notes 1419-1422; scene wwwroot/data/scenes/MACHINE-SHOP.json): 7 x 3.6 x 8, as wide as Mech Corridor South north of it. North, on the axis, the 2.4 x 2.8 doorway onto Mech Corridor South; west and east, 1.6 x 2.4 doorways 0.64 m north of the middle, where they meet the Tool Room's and the Robot Shop's doorways. No doors. The chemical dispenser against the rear (south) wall on the axis, and "a variety of unusual machines" (compone.zil 1640-1641) in the four corners: a mill (north-west), a vat with a pipe to the ceiling (north-east), a lathe (south-west) and a press (south-east). The openings and exits are on the walls' inner faces (x +-3.5, z -4). No globals (world.json MACHINE-SHOP globals []); one scenery word, SPOUT.

The eye is [0, 1.6, -0.4], 0.4 m north of the middle on the axis (the scene file gives no eye, so the metadata's is the one the renders and the game use: wwwroot/scene/design.js 15). Why: from the middle no clean four-view ring exists (the search is in the plan note below). The eye stands 2.1 m or more from every machine, in no door's sweep (the room has no doors), and still on the axis, so the line north is seen straight on. From it the side doorways are 0.24 m north of abeam, the north doorway 3.6 m off and the dispenser's face 3.6 m.

Norm plan (DR-106, fabric renders reference/DR-106_MACHINE-SHOP-{072,162,252,342,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-072/162/252/342, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 131, 1254 square, all from the eye. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 29.60 degrees above and below level at its lowest (bearing 27), so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 24.60) = 130.8, rounded up to 131. Spans 90/90/90/90, so the seam windows are 115-119, 205-209, 295-299 and 25-29 (each lo 43, hi 47). 115-119 is on the east wall's south half: 3.5 degrees from the press (122.5), 15.9 from the east doorway's south jamb (99.1), 22.5 from the south-east corner (141.5). 205-209 is on the south wall west of the dispenser: 6.6 from its west end and button strip (198.4), 4.3 from the lathe's far end (213.3), 9.5 from the south-west corner (218.5). 295-299 is on the west wall: 8.5 from the west doorway's north jamb (286.5), 4.1 from the mill (303.1), 16.8 from the north-west corner (315.8). 25-29 is on the north wall: 6.6 from the north doorway's east jamb (18.4), 5.8 from the vat (34.8), 15.2 from the north-east corner (44.2). Each window is plain wall top to bottom over the level views' height there (29.6 degrees either side of level, 45 degrees off centre); the ceiling lamps are higher (31 degrees up and more) and belong to the UP cap. Each opening is whole inside one view's share: the north doorway (341.6-18.4) in 342, the east doorway (73.5-99.1) in 072, the west doorway (260.9-286.5) in 252; the dispenser with its buttons, spout and grate (161.6-198.4) is whole in 162. Seeds 162 and 342; 072 and 252 are built from them, the caps last. The search (Norm, 15 Sep; plan geometry of the fabric's corners, openings and machines, each window required on plain wall 6 degrees or more from every corner and opening edge and off every machine): from the middle, no four-view ring at one lens anywhere in 100-120 (bearings every 1 degree) qualifies, and five views qualify only at 106-108, with windows 1 degree wide. The machines stand in the four corners and the doorways and the dispenser mid-wall, leaving eight strips of plain wall 5-19 degrees wide, and a 110-degree view's two windows end 94 degrees apart. Moving the eye north along the axis (every 0.05 m from -0.8 to 0, 90-degree rings every 0.1 degree, lenses 108, 110 and 112), -0.4 gives the widest clearances at 110; 072/162/252/342 are its whole-degree bearings. No window needs an exception.

The nine buttons, in the order the game lists them (compone.zil 1653-1659) and left to right as the player faces the dispenser (looking south, so east is on the left): red, blue, green, yellow (KUULINTS 1 - 4), gray, brown, black (KATALISTS 1 - 3), the square white BAAS and the round white ASID, from x 0.8 to x -0.8 (objects). The fabric's placeholder colours run the other way: its four warning-red boxes are at the west end, the viewer's right (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1199; DR-106_MACHINE-SHOP-162_FABRIC.png). Paint the metadata's order; the pick targets follow it.

No painted variants: no door, no structural state, no power state, and the ladder across the rift left out. Overlays: the thing under the spout (THING-UNDER-SPOUT), the dispenser's damage (DISPENSER-DAMAGED), Floyd and dropped items; the base paintings show none of them (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.3). Neither: the fluid that pours, splashes and dries up (compone.zil 1795-1796, 1811-1812) and Floyd's button-pushing (1660-1668) are moments of text, not states; the CHEMICAL-FLAG colour (1773) has nothing to show.

Engine, not this metadata: the ladder can be extended here (the game refuses only in Storage East and West, Booth 2 and the elevators, compone.zil 668-671; rules/kalamontee.js 279), and an 8 m ladder has no clear floor to lie on in this 7 x 8 m room between the machines and the dispenser. FLOYD.label: robot
FLOYD.notes: Starts here, switched off (compone.zil 1838-1848; world.json FLOYD.location ROBOT-SHOP): "Only one robot, about four feet high, looks even remotely close to being in working order" (FDESC 1841-1843), and EXAMINE: "The de-activated robot is leaning against the wall, its head lolling to the side" (compone.zil 2074-2078; port rules/floyd.js 238). So until he first comes alive he stands against the pier between the two doorways: the box's centre, his back 0.02 m off the pier's face (x -4), in the middle of the pier (z -1.59), 4.05 m from the eye at bearing 293.1, whole in TURN-289 and between the two doorways (1.46 m from the north-west lane and 2.2 m from the west lane). Size is the switched-off cutout's: 1.22 m ("about four feet"), 0.51 m wide, 0.5 m footprint (wwwroot/data/characters.json FLOYD variant "FLOYD without RLANDBIT", FLOYD-OFF.png). The place holds until TOUCHBIT (graybox.js 190; design.js 57), which the game sets only when he comes alive (FLOYD-COMES-ALIVE, compone.zil 2153-2155; floyd.js 115). From then on he stands at actors.FLOYD. Never painted: the base paintings show the pier bare (ARTWORK-BRIEF 3.3).

DEVICES-PSEUDO.label: devices

EXAMINE: "They are components of disassembled robots, beyond repair." (globals.zil 2559-2562.) One tag, over the round torso and the head on the east bench and the bench top between them (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1234, 1236-1237): x 3.1 to 3.7, y 0.9 (the bench top) to 1.6, z -1.09 to 2.41, bearings 70.6-127.9, whole inside TURN-115's share (68.5-155) and crossed by no seam window. The exception, and the search behind it. The racks fill the south wall from 144.3 to 212.2, within 3 degrees of each south corner's 6-degree margin (147.34 and 212.66), so a seam on the south wall crosses them; the only way round is a south view owning 135.3-224.7, and at lens 110 that pins the west view to 271.7-276.3, whose seam with the next view then falls within 6 degrees of the north-west corner or inside the north-west doorway. An exhaustive search (scratch caster over scenes/ROBOT-SHOP.json; every ring of four and of five level views, each lens 100-120, view centres on whole degrees, windows by solveSeams, each doorway whole inside one view): no ring at any lens keeps every window 6 degrees clear of the corners and doorway jambs AND off every tall fitting (the cabinet, the half-built robot, the three things on the bench, the racks); at lenses 100-106 no four-view ring even clears the corners and jambs. The rings whose only crossing is the racks' boards are four-view rings at lenses 108-111 alone (5, 35, 137 and 279 of them); the best at each keeps its other windows 0.5, 1.0, 1.6 and 1.4 degrees clear of the nearest tall fitting, and lens 110's best is this ring (22/115/196/289 and its 1-degree neighbours). The other lens-110 family, 58/151/233/325, crosses the racks mid-bay (8 degrees from the uprights) but puts its east window 1.5 degrees from the round torso and its north window 1.9 from the half-built robot, and splits the two doorways between two views; this one keeps both doorways, the pier and Floyd in one view. So: four views at lens 110, one seam across the racks' east bay. Paint that bay's boards plainly near 149-162 (README, Look).

States. No painted variants: no door, no structural state, no sky, no power state, and nothing seen through either doorway changes. STAIR-DOORWAY.beyond: REACTOR-ACCESS-STAIRS: "A dark stairway winds downward" (compone.zil 1454). The 1.4 x 2.3 doorway at bearings 8.5-26.6, 4.21 m from the eye to its centre, no door; it opens into a 3.6 m square concrete shaft north of this room, a steel spiral round a post on the shaft's axis, which lies 6.29 m off at bearing 18.6 -- the doorway is on the line from this eye to it (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1103-1121, 1291-1313). Nothing else: the treads below those two, the shaft's side walls and roof and its foot, 16.6 m down, are out of sight. Dark: the shaft has no light of its own (no ONBIT, compone.zil 1477), and the stair's own paintings are lit by the lamp the player carries in there, which from here is not in it. So from this room only this room's lamps reach it: the sill, the two treads and the near face of the post catch a little of this room's light, and past them the shaft falls away to black, darkest downward. The fabric renders show its far wall a dim grey from the scene's lamps and ambient; paint it darker than that. Nothing seen here changes with the game. Derive the stair's steel and concrete from the Reactor Access Stairs' package once it has art; no Floyd, no loose items.

CONTROLS.label: set of controls
CONTROLS.notes: "This room contains many dials and gauges for controlling a massive planetary power reactor" (compone.zil 1451-1452); CONTROLS (globals.zil 243-249: synonyms CONTRO, PANEL, DIALS, GAUGES; adjectives CONTRO, COMPLEX), a local global of this room (1465).
