notes: DR-106 metadata by Norm (the user's decision, 14 Sep), from the one Kalamontee layout (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs: the room 1102, 1107 and 1135, its fittings 1251-1272, the elevator door 1273-1279, the car 1108 and 1280-1290, the stair shaft 1103-1121 and 1291-1313, lamps 1335, thresholds 1352 and 1359-1360, the scene 1387 and its note 1427-1430; wwwroot/data/scenes/REACTOR-CONTROL.json). 8 x 3.6 x 8, origin on the floor at the room's centre, x east, z south; frame centre [180.76, 0, 25.32] in the Mess Corridor's frame. West, the 1.2 x 2.25 doorway onto the Mech Corridor on the wall's middle. East, 0.5 m south of the middle, the reactor elevator's 2 x 2.5 metal door in a 0.12 m frame, with the button on a plate 0.18 m north of the frame. North, 1.3 m east of the middle, the 1.4 x 2.3 doorway into the stair shaft (exit DOWN). Fittings: the south console bank (desk, raised panel and gauge wall, 5.6 m long), the north console under the diagram on the north wall's west half, two gauge panels on the west wall either side of the doorway, one on the east wall south of the door with a cabinet under it. Nothing starts here (world.json REACTOR-CONTROL objects []), and nothing here is moved by the rules, so there are no objects and no largeObjects.

The eye is the layout's, [0, 1.6, 0], the middle of the room: 3.1 m from the desk's front and 3.25 m from the north console, clear of every fitting, and the door's leaves slide into the walls, so there is no sweep to keep out of. The stair doorway was placed on the line from this eye to the shaft's axis (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1105-1107), so that the stair itself is seen dropping away past the post.

Norm plan (DR-106, 15 Sep; fabric renders reference/DR-106_REACTOR-CONTROL-{080,161,254,347,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png with the door shut, the base, and reference/DR-106_REACTOR-CONTROL-080_FABRIC-DOOR-OPEN.png): TURN-080/161/254/347, pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 133, 1254 square; all from the eye. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 28.95 degrees above and below level at its lowest (bearing 33.5), so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 23.95) = 132.1, rounded up to 133. Spans 81/93/93/93, each under 94. Seam windows (turn.js solveSeams: lo = max(8, span - 47), hi = min(span - 8, 47)): 33-34, 114-127, 207-208 and 300-301. 33-34 is on plain north wall (x 2.60-2.70), 6.4 degrees from the stair doorway's east jamb (26.6), 11.0 from the north-east corner and 29.2 from the button. 114-127 crosses the east wall's gauge panel (105.4-131.8; on it z 1.76-2.98) and the cabinet under it (105.6-136.3): 8.6 from the panel's north end, 4.8 from its south end, 8.0 from the south-east corner, 15.0 from the door's frame. 207-208 crosses the south console bank's gauge wall (144.5-215.5; on it x -2.00 to -2.08) between the fabric's two westmost dials (202.8-205.5 and 211.0-213.3), 7.5 from its west end, 14.1 from the desk's west end and 17.0 from the south-west corner. 300-301 crosses the north-west gauge panel (288.1-308.3; on it z -2.28 to -2.37), 11.9 from its south end, 7.3 from its north end, 14.0 from the north-west corner, 21.5 from the west doorway and 22.0 from the diagram. Each opening is whole inside one view: the stair doorway (8.5-26.6) in 347, the elevator door with its frame and the button (63.2-99.0) in 080, the west doorway (261.5-278.5) in 254; the diagram (323.0-2.9) is whole in 347. TURN-080 is the base (REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR without OPENBIT) and owns TURN-080@DOOR-OPEN; no other view sees the door. TURN-080's left rim (bearing 25) also takes in the stair doorway's east jamb, outside its share. audit-turns proposes 003/093/183/273 from the openings alone; its seam windows (46-50, 136-140, 226-230, 316-320) lie 1-5 degrees from the four corners, on the ends of the cabinet, the desk, the south-west panel and the north console, so it is not taken.

The seam search, and the exception it leaves (Norm, 15 Sep). The room's fittings leave plain wall wide enough for a seam window 6 degrees clear on both sides only in the north-east: 32.6-39.0 on the north wall and 51.0-57.3 on the east. Every other stretch between a corner, an opening and a fitting is under 12 degrees wide. So a scratch search went over every ring of four and of five level views at whole-degree bearings, at lenses 100, 105, 110, 115 and 120, from this eye, keeping each ring whose every seam window is 6 degrees or more from the four corners, the three openings (the elevator door with its frame), the button plate and the diagram. It found 2448 four-view rings, all at lens 110, none at 100, 105, 115 or 120; and five-view rings at 105 (7555), 110 (202,400) and 120 (1905). Every ring, of four or of five, has at least three seam windows on eye-level gauge panels (every four-view ring exactly three), so crossing panels cannot be avoided. Among the four-view rings the best by distance from every edge (corner, opening or fitting) is this one, 080/161/254/347: its worst window edge is 4.8 degrees from a panel's end (the east panel's south end) and 6.4 from a hard edge (the stair doorway's jamb). The only other ring on that front, 081/162/255/348, trades these for 3.8 and 7.0. The same search from eyes 0.8 m off the middle (x and z each -0.8, 0 or 0.8) found no eye whose rings cross fewer than three panels, except rings that put a window within 0.2 degrees of a panel's end, which is worse. The best of them, [0.8, 1.6, 0], gives 074/165/248/341 with every window 10.3 degrees from the hard edges and 8.3 from every panel end. It is not taken, because it moves the eye off the line the layout set the stair doorway on and off the layout's 'eye at the middle' (the scene's note). Accepted as the exception: three seam windows cross gauge panels, each on the panel's face and clear of its ends. The painter keeps a plain vertical joint in each panel on those bands (see the paint note below). The DR-106 rule of 6 degrees from corners, opening edges and artwork holds for every corner, opening, the button and the diagram.

For the painting. The seams cross the gauge panels, so each crossed panel wants a plain vertical joint, or a gap between two sections of dials, on its seam band: the east panel between z 1.76 and 2.98 (with the cabinet's front under it between z 1.49 and 2.52), the south gauge wall between x -1.9 and -2.2 (no dial there), and the north-west panel between z -2.28 and -2.37. Keep the fittings where the fabric draws them, since each seam runs across one: the console bank, the four panels, the cabinet and the north console. Keep also the elevator door's frame, its leaves' meeting line and the button plate (the variant is cut against them, and the button's proxy is on the plate), and the diagram board (its proxy). The painted lamps keep to the south half of the ceiling.

Seeds first: TURN-161 (the south console bank with its dials, the east panel and cabinet, the south-east corner: the room's 'many dials and gauges') and TURN-347 (the diagram over the north console, the north-west corner, and the stair doorway with the dark shaft, the top treads and the post). The two do not overlap. TURN-080 (the elevator door, the button, the north-east corner) and TURN-254 (the west doorway onto the Mech Corridor, the south-west panel) each lie between them and are built from both. Then TURN-080@DOOR-OPEN from the accepted TURN-080, and the caps last.

States: DOOR-SHUT is the base, DOOR-OPEN a painted variant owned by TURN-080 alone, Floyd and dropped items overlays. Nothing else the eye sees changes. The room is ONBIT (compone.zil 1463), so its lamps are always on. The car never moves and is always lit (compone.zil 1512, 2607-2649; rules/connectors.js 238-259). The Mech Corridor has no states. The stair shaft is always dark from here. No rule touches this room's fittings or the reactor: CONTROLS only refuses (globals.zil 251-272), and the Systems Monitors' REEAKTURZ monitor is green in every state (compone.zil 1131-1161). No sky: every ray through the three doorways ends on the Mech Corridor's west wall, the car's walls or the shaft's concrete, and the UP cap sees only this ceiling. So no day phase and no sun.

Engine, not this metadata: the ladder can be extended here (canon refuses only in Storage East and West, Booth 2 and the upper and lower elevators, compone.zil 666-671; rules/kalamontee.js 279) and cannot then be carried (compone.zil 650-653). An 8 m ladder has no clear floor to lie on in this 8 m room with its console bank. Where an extended ladder goes in a room is for the engine to settle, as in the Conference Room; nothing is painted for it.

At the doorway's east jamb, 164.4-164.8 and 15 degrees up, a 0.4-degree sliver of the gauge panel on its east wall at that wall's south end (fabric 1266), 9.9-10.1 m off; the rest of the east wall is out of sight. Out of sight: Reactor Control's floor and its consoles' desks and faces, the diagram (DIAGRAM-PSEUDO, on its north wall behind this doorway, fabric 1262-1264), its west door and the Mech Corridor, its west lamp, and the reactor elevator's metal door and its button (on the east wall, 2.4 m and more north of the sliver; no ray reaches them, the door open or shut, since the stair's scene carries no leaf). No sky: no ray from the eye leaves the fabric (every 0.5 degree over the sphere, and 0.05 over the doorway, with the elevator door shut and open). Nothing seen here changes with the game: Reactor Control's lamps are on at all hours (ONBIT) and the elevator door is out of sight. In the fabric Reactor Control's ceiling renders near-black (its lamps hang flush on it and do not light it); paint it as that room's own painting paints its ceiling, lit by its fluorescents. Derive from Reactor Control's package once it has art; no Floyd, no loose items.
REACTOR-CONTROL-DOORWAY.notes: UP (compone.zil 1476) leaves through this doorway, climbing the stair's last eleven treads clockwise round the post from the eye's tread to the top one inside the sill; Reactor Control's DOWN (compone.zil 1462) comes in through it, so it is that room's north opening, 1.3 m east of the middle of its north wall (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1107, 1135). The position is the opening's centre on the shaft wall's inner face (z 1.8). Below the sill a deck plate, the fabric's threshold slab in the walls' depth (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1360), closes the slit between the two rooms' floors; it is hidden from this eye behind the sill.

UP.notes: To REACTOR-CONTROL through the south doorway (compone.zil 1476); a plain direct exit (world.json REACTOR-ACCESS-STAIRS.exits), no door. The climb takes 30 (C-MOVE, compone.zil 1471-1474; world.json moveTime UP 30; engine/core.js 425), where an ordinary move takes 20 (core.js 23). graybox.js 153, 158 and 164 draw UP as its tilted hatch at this position, in the doorway. The same 1.4 x 2.3 m hole as Reactor Control's north doorway (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1135).

DOWN.notes: No opening: the stair winds on down, and DOWN leads back into this same room (compone.zil 1475). The panel is graybox.js's 1.4 x 1.4 floor hatch (154, 159, 164), laid over the next steps down from the eye's tread -- counter-clockwise round the post, west and south-west of it (the treads at bearings 245-267.5 from the shaft's axis, 0.4-0.6 m under the eye's tread) -- 1.1 m out from the axis, clear of the post; seen only in the DOWN cap (60 degrees down, bearing 193 from the eye). Canon: going down from this dark room into itself with no light is a move from dark to dark, and the grue takes the player 75 times in 100 (core.js 164; the source's odds); with the lamp the player simply arrives here again.

STAIRS.label: stairway
STAIRS.notes: The room's one local global (compone.zil 1478; globals.zil 49-53: synonyms STAIRS STEPS GANGWAY STAIRWAY, DESC "stairway"). No action routine of its own in the source; the port's STAIRS handler (wwwroot/rules/ship.js 133) sends CLIMB UP, CLIMB ON and THROUGH to UP (Reactor Control) and CLIMB DOWN to DOWN (this room again). The proxy is the stair where the ring shows it best: the three treads rising past the post's east side (bearings 65-110 from the shaft's axis, 1.0-1.4 m over the eye's tread; x 0.3-1.7, z -0.8 to 0.6, y 0.8-1.5), seen from the eye at bearings 83-141 and 2-38 degrees down, in TURN-058's right and TURN-161's left; its southern part lies behind the post, which is the stair's too. Clear of the UP hatch in the doorway and the DOWN hatch west of the post.

constraints: stand on the eye's own tread, the only floor at y 0 (graybox.js 270-271 and 279 stand every actor on y 0)
keep the UP and DOWN lanes and the dropped-item anchors clear
FLOYD.notes: Floyd follows the player into any room 80 times in 100 (rules/floyd.js 304-306; compone.zil 2187-2195), dark rooms included; the room has no FLOYDBIT (compone.zil 1477), so he never goes off exploring from here (floyd.js 296). graybox.js 176-177 draws him only while the room is lit, which is the light the paintings show. His spot is the outer end of the eye's tread, 1.6 m out from the axis at bearing 312.5 -- the only place clear of both lanes (0.60 m from each) where the engine draws him standing on a step: graybox.js stands every actor's feet on y 0 whatever the metadata's y (270-271, 279), and only the eye's tread is at y 0 (the others step 0.2 m a tread). From the eye he is 0.6 m off at bearing 312.6, his head 32 degrees down: the top of him at the foot of TURN-315, the rest in the DOWN cap. Overlay, never painted.

droppedItems.notes: Floor points on the treads next to the eye's, 0.08 m over each tread's top (the tops step 0.2 m a tread: y = (n + 1) x 0.2 - 13.8 for tread n counted from the foot, fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1119, 1310; parts.js 810-815): the tread one up (n 69, bearing 335 from the axis, 1.35 m out), one down (n 67, bearing 290, 1.6 m out), two up (n 70, bearing 357.5, 1.4 m out) and three up (n 71, bearing 20, 1.4 m out). Each is 0.57 m or more from both lanes (the lanes run south from the eye; these lie north and west of it), 0.62 m or more from Floyd, and off the DOWN hatch. The eye's own tread, the one floor at y 0, has room only for Floyd outside the lanes. Engine item, not worked around: graybox.js stands every dropped thing on y 0 whatever the anchor's y (270-271, 279), so today these draw 0.2-0.6 m off their treads; the y is given for when the engine stands a floor thing on its anchor's height. Overlays, drawn only while the room is lit (graybox.js 176-177).

changes: Neither painted nor overlaid: the engine's. The paintings are the room lit by the lamp the player carries; there is no dark painting and no lamp-lit variant. Unlit, the game prints "It is pitch black. You might be eaten by a grue." (verbs.zil 68-73; engine/core.js 172-175) and graybox.js draws only the exits the player already knows (graybox.js 120, 176-177; parser.js 373).
DARK.notes: The room has no ONBIT (compone.zil 1477). A room is lit by its own ONBIT or by a lit thing the player carries or that stands in it (LIT?, parser.zil 1213-1228; lit(), engine/core.js 149-158), and the game's one such thing is the Radiation Lab's powerful portable lamp (LAMP, comptwo.zil 2186-2195; LAMP-F sets ONBIT, 2197-2210). LIT is worked out on entry and every turn (core.js 163, 411). Coming down from lit Reactor Control is safe; DOWN from here in the dark is a dark-to-dark move, 75 in 100 fatal (core.js 164).

changes: Neither for the light: the paintings keep the carried lamp's light, from about the eye, wherever a set-down lamp stands. The lamp itself is a dropped thing, an overlay at its anchor.
LAMP-SET-DOWN.notes: A lit lamp standing in the room still lights it (core.js 157); the paintings cannot move their light to an anchor, so they do not try (the Transportation Supply's rule, TRANSPORTATION-SUPPLY.metadata.json lighting.notes).

changes: Neither: the reactor elevator's door, in Reactor Control's east wall, is out of this eye's sight open or shut (cast every 0.1 degree through the doorway: all any ray reaches of that wall is a 0.4-degree sliver of the gauge panel at its south end, 2.4 m south of the door's south jamb). The paintings are right in both states.
ELEVATOR-DOOR-OPEN.notes: The button opens it (REACTOR-BUTTON-PSEUDO, rules/connectors.js 521-525; globals.zil 2635-2640) and I-REACTOR-DOOR-CLOSE shuts it 30 turns later once the player is out of the car (connectors.js 430-437; compone.zil 1492-1498). The car itself never moves (its buttons do nothing, connectors.js 243), so there is no elevator position to show.

changes: Overlay: Floyd's cutout at actors.FLOYD, on the eye's tread; never painted.
FLOYD-PRESENT.notes: He follows the player here (rules/floyd.js 304-306) and is drawn only while the room is lit (graybox.js 176-177).

lighting.notes: No fixture and no light of the room's own (no ONBIT, compone.zil 1477). The paintings show the shaft lit by the portable lamp the player carries, the only thing that can light it (LAMP, comptwo.zil 2186-2210; lit(), core.js 149-158): a warm light from about the eye, falling off fast down the well and up to the roof, no lamp drawn. The scene draws it as a light with no housing 0.1 m over the eye (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1314-1317: #FFD6A0, intensity 20, reach 6 m), so the roof 4.2 m up and the stair more than a turn down (3.2 m) fall into darkness; the bottom of the fabric's shaft, 16 m down, is only there to close the scene -- paint the well going down into the dark. Through the doorway, Reactor Control's warm fluorescents (on at all hours, ONBIT, compone.zil 1463), from its own package. The fabric casts no shadows, so some of that room's lamplight reaches the shaft's walls through the concrete: paint the carried lamp's light only. Not a sky room: no ray from the eye reaches the sky, so no DAY-PHASE, no lighting.sun and no entry in SHARED-ROOM-METADATA sky.rooms. Dry concrete and steel: no wet, flicker or flood artwork.

notes: DR-106 layout (scripts/fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1103-1121 the stair and the eye, 1135-1137 the rooms, 1291-1313 the shaft, 1314-1317 the lamp, 1360 the threshold, 1388 and 1431-1434 the scene; wwwroot/data/scenes/REACTOR-ACCESS-STAIRS.json). A steel spiral stair in a 3.6 m square concrete shaft north of Reactor Control: a post 0.5 m across on the shaft's axis, floor to roof; 80 treads, 0.2 m a rise, 16 a turn, each a flat steel plate 1.53 x 0.40 x 0.08 m running out from the post to 1.78 m (parts.js 803-818), five turns in all, rising clockwise; the top tread (n 79) is level with Reactor Control's floor at bearing 200 from the axis, just inside the doorway behind a 0.3 m sill; going down from it the stair turns east across the doorway's front and on round the north. No railing, no landing. The frame: the shaft's axis at the level of the eye's tread (n 68), which is 2.2 m under Reactor Control's floor; the room's box is the shaft from that tread (y 0) to the roof (5.8), the walls running on down to the shaft's bottom (y -14.4). The doorway, 1.4 x 2.3, is in the south wall from x -1.4 to 0, its sill at y 2.2.

Why the eye is off the axis: the post stands on it. The eye stands on the eye's tread (n 68, bearing 312.5 from the axis), 1 m out from the post, 1.6 m over the tread: nothing overhead (the stair ends eleven treads up, at the doorway, before it comes round over the eye again), clear of every tread's edge, and its sightline up to the doorway clears the post by 0.48 m (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1114-1118). From the eye the post fills bearings 118.2-146.8 (0.75 m to its face) and hides the south-east corner (134.3); the other corners are at 66.2 (north-east), 203.3 (south-west) and 316.6 (north-west). The north and west walls are 1.12 and 1.06 m from the eye, the east and south 2.54 and 2.48 m.

Norm plan (DR-106, fabric renders reference/DR-106_REACTOR-ACCESS-STAIRS-{058,161,264,315,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-058/161/264/315, pitch 0, HFOV 120, 1672x941 -- one lens, 120 for the tightest room in the wing (two walls 1.1 m off, the post 0.75 m) and the only lens that fits the plan (below); caps UP/DOWN at bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 128, 1254 square, all from the eye [-0.737, 1.6, -0.676]. The caps' lens is the one scripts/underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (run with the four fabric renders as --from, output to scratch): the ring reaches 31.3 degrees up and down at its lowest (lib/views.mjs ringReach), so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 26.3) = 127.5, rounded up to 128. Spans 103/103/51/103. Seam windows (wwwroot/dashboard/turn.js solveSeams, margin 8): 6-7 (north wall), 109-110 (east wall), 212-213 and 272-307 (west wall). Clearances: 6-7 is 49.4 degrees from the north-west corner and 59.2 from the north-east, plain north wall top to bottom in both frames; 109-110 is 8.2 from the post's north limb (118.2) and 42.8 from the north-east corner; 212-213 is 8.7 from the south-west corner and 17.0 from the doorway's west jamb (195.0), plain west wall; 272-307 is 9.6 from the north-west corner and 68.7 from the south-west, plain west wall. The doorway (163.4-195.0), the post (118.2-146.8) and the stair's top treads are whole inside 161 in bearing. The doorway's head is 47.5-49.5 degrees up, above any level view at lens 100-120 (a 120 reaches 44.3 at its centre, 161 reaches 38.9-44.3 over the doorway), so the UP cap carries the head: over the doorway it reaches down to 25.0-26.0, and there it is built from 161's pixels (underpaint.mjs caps), so the two agree where they overlap.

Accepted exception (Norm, DR-106): the 109-110 window crosses the outer ends of two treads (n 73 and 74, 1.0-1.4 m off, 9.5-33.5 degrees down), with plain east wall above them. The search, with the windows as solveSeams computes them, each required to keep 6 degrees from the three visible corners, the doorway's jambs and the post's limbs and never to fall inside the doorway or the post: every ring of 4 views at integer bearings at lens 100, 105, 110 and 115-120, and of 5 views at 100, 110, 115 and 120. Plain wall -- nothing but one wall face inside either frame's reach at the seam -- runs only from 209.3 round the west and north to 42: the east wall has the rising treads in its lower half at every bearing (73-117), and the south wall between the post and the doorway has treads up to 31 degrees up. So the 167 degrees from 42 to 209.3, holding the post and the doorway, need a seam between them on the east or the south wall, over treads. No 4-view ring at 100-115 exists at all (the view holding the post and the doorway must span 97 degrees or more between its seams, and a lens L allows L - 16); at 116-120 1,260 rings exist (299 distinct), every one with exactly one window over treads, and this ring has the widest clearance (8.2). Five views do no better: two windows over treads at 100-115, one at 120. Considered and not taken: a seam down the post's face (4 views at 110, 082/175/260/349, window 128-129, clearance 9.6), which splits the post between two views through the lamp's highlight on it and moves the doorway's view off the post. Here the post, the doorway and the top treads stay whole in 161, and 058 is built from 161, so it carries 161's own pixels over the crossing (brief 2.1). scripts/audit-turns.mjs, which plans from the openings alone, proposes 089/179/269/359 at 110; its windows would put one on the post (132-136) and one on the north-west corner (312-316).

Seeds first: TURN-161 (the post, the stair rising round it to the doorway, the doorway and Reactor Control beyond, the south-west corner) and TURN-315 (the bare north-west corner and the two nearest walls, 1.1 m off). TURN-058 and TURN-264 are built from both (058 overlaps 161 on 101-118 and 315 on 358-15; 264 overlaps 161 on 204-221 and 315 on 255-324), the caps last from all four.

What each view shows (fabric renders): 058 -- the north-east corner at 8 degrees right of centre, the north and east walls, the treads rising round the north-east and east from the bottom of the frame to its right edge (n 70-75), the post just out of frame right; 161 -- the ends of treads 72-75 at its left edge, the post left of centre (tread 76 behind it), treads 77-79 rising right of it to the doorway top right of centre with Reactor Control's ceiling and lamp through it, the south-west corner 42 degrees right; 264 -- the bare west wall, the north-west corner 53 degrees right; 315 -- the north-west corner 2 degrees right of centre, the two nearest walls; UP -- the shaft rising 4.2 m to its roof, the post rising to it on the south-east, the doorway at the top edge (south) with Reactor Control beyond, the stair's top treads seen from under them; DOWN -- the spiral winding down round the post, the eye's tread and its neighbours nearest, the well going down into the dark.

No painted variants: no door (world.json REACTOR-ACCESS-STAIRS doors []), no structural state, no sky, and nothing beyond the doorway that changes (Reactor Control's lamps always on, the elevator door out of sight). DARK is the engine's, LAMP-SET-DOWN keeps the carried lamp's light, Floyd and dropped things are overlays. The stair is fixed and no rule moves it, so no largeObjects. No object starts here (world.json objects [], no pseudo words); STAIRS is the one global. The base paintings show no portable objects, no Floyd and no lamp.

REACTOR-CONTROL-DOOR.beyond: REACTOR-CONTROL, through the car's own door, always open from in here (states.DOOR-OPEN): the 2 x 2.5 hole west, the same hole as Reactor Control's EAST (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1135-1136), 0.16 m deep (the car's wall, x -2.1 to -2.18, and Reactor Control's, -2.18 to -2.26), its centre 2.1 m straight west. Measured on the fabric (scenes/REACTOR-ELEVATOR.json, cast from the eye every 0.1 degree; DR-106_REACTOR-ELEVATOR-257_FABRIC.png); distances in plan from the eye, to an opening's centre where an opening is given. The door spans bearings 244.54-295.46, 23.2 degrees up to its head and 37.3 down to its sill on the axis; all of it is in TURN-257, whose bottom edge cuts the sill north of bearing 277 (the DOWN cap has the whole sill). In the doorway: the reveal's two faces, and on Reactor Control's side the inner faces of the frame round the door (band 0.12, 0.1 m proud of that room's east wall, fabric 1270), 2.26-2.56 m off, at 246.2-247.0 and 293.0-293.8 and under the head; the threshold slab in the sill (fabric 1359). Beyond: Reactor Control's deck from the sill to its west wall; its ceiling, with the housing of its west lamp at bearings 254.6-258.0, 12-14 degrees up, 7.9-9.1 m off (the fabric's lamps are placeholders: Reactor Control's own paintings place its fixtures); its west wall, 10.26 m off, over nearly its whole 8 m width (bearings 247.1-288.8) and its whole height (8.8 degrees down to 11.0 up). In the middle of that wall the doorway onto the Mech Corridor, 1.2 x 2.25, doorless, centred 10.27 m off at bearing 267.2 (263.9-270.6; 3.6 degrees up to 8.9 down), with its threshold slab (fabric 1352); either side of it a gauge panel 1.8 wide, 1.2-2.4 m up (fabric 1265): the south one at 250.6-260.0, the north one at 274.5-284.3, 10.2-10.8 m off. Right of that, at bearings 286.6-292.9, 7.1-9.9 m off, the west end of the console bank under the diagram on the north wall (compone.zil 1451-1452; fabric 1262-1264): the desk's front and top over nearly its whole 3.2 m, and above it the west 1.0 m of the diagram, 1.4-2.7 m up, at 290.6-292.9 (the rest of it is past the door's north jamb), and the north wall's plain west end over it. At the far left, bearings 247.1-248.3, 9.3-9.7 m off, a sliver of the base of the south console bank's west end (its gauges and indicators out of sight). Through the Mech Corridor doorway (bearings 264.0-270.5): the Mech Corridor's deck from 10.46 m and its bare west wall, 14.82 m off, from the floor to 2.5 m (the doorway's head cuts it, so no ceiling), 0.37-2.06 m south of that hall's middle: the Physical Plant's south-east exit, 2 m north of the middle, is out of sight. Also out of sight from here: the button beside the elevator door and the door's shut leaves (both on Reactor Control's side of the wall; the leaves are drawn only in its scene, fabric 1273-1279), the stair doorway (bearings 301.7-309.4 from this eye, past the north jamb), the gauge panel and cabinet on Reactor Control's east wall, and its east lamp. No sky anywhere. The caps (HFOV 133): DOWN takes the sill and Reactor Control's deck to 3.68 m from the eye (1.42 m past that room's wall face) and nothing else; UP does not reach the door (its head is 66.8 degrees from the zenith, the cap's edge 66.5). TURN-350's left edge (295.0) takes 0.46 degrees of the north jamb's reveal and nothing beyond it. Nothing seen through the door changes with the game: the door is open whenever the player is here, Reactor Control's elevator door is seen only from its own side, and the Mech Corridor has no doors. No people, no loose items and no Floyd in the glimpse. Derive from Reactor Control's and the Mech Corridor's own packages once they have art.
REACTOR-CONTROL-DOOR.notes: WEST and OUT (compone.zil 1510-1511) share this one hole, the same hole as Reactor Control's EAST and IN (1460-1461), which there are conditional on REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR; from in here they are direct. Scene: shell opening WEST [0, 1.25, 2, 2.5] (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1136); the car is centred on the door, 0.5 m south of Reactor Control's middle (EZ, fabric 1103-1108). From the eye the hole spans bearings 244.54-295.46. Threshold: a floor slab in the two walls' depth, the door's width, level with both floors (fabric 1359), so the sill reads as floor. Paint it as floor.

WEST.notes: To REACTOR-CONTROL, direct (compone.zil 1510); OUT (1511) is the same opening and folds into this panel. It matches Reactor Control's 2 x 2.5 EAST (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1135). The REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR hangs in it but is open whenever the player is here (states.DOOR-OPEN), so the car's way out is never shut.

CONTROLS.label: set of controls
CONTROLS.notes: The control panel of the room description (compone.zil 1504-1505; CONTROLS, synonyms CONTRO PANEL DIALS GAUGES, globals.zil 243-249). EXAMINE: "The control panel is a simple one, as described. Just a small slot and two buttons." (globals.zil 251-257; kalamontee.js 90-91). The fabric's panel exactly: 0.6 wide, 0.7 high (y 0.95-1.65), x -1.5 to -0.9 on the north wall, 0.05 out (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1284), its west edge 0.6 m from the door's wall; bearings 319.3-332.7 from the eye, inside TURN-350 alone and in neither cap. The proxy is the panel's back 0.04 m, so the button and slot proxies stand clear in front of it. It carries the two buttons, the slot and (a proposal) one slim dark sign strip, nothing else; the fabric's control-face texture (a keypad and a display) is a placeholder material, not a layout.

ELEVATOR-BUTTON.label: button
ELEVATOR-BUTTON.notes: "an Up button, a Down button" (compone.zil 1504-1505): one object, ELEVATOR-BUTTON, "button" (compone.zil 2587-2592), whose menu offers Push Up and Push Down (connectors.js 580), so one proxy covers both, as in the Upper and Lower Elevators: the fabric's Up button [-1.35, 1.45] over its Down button [-1.35, 1.2], each 0.1 square and 0.03 proud (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1285-1286), bearings 320.9-323.0. The car never moves: either button answers "Nothing happens." (ELEVATOR-BUTTON-F moves only the upper and lower cars, compone.zil 2607-2645) and the port adds "The slot beside the buttons stays dark." here (connectors.js 241-243, a user-approved deviation); a bare "push button" asks which (compone.zil 2646-2649; connectors.js 258). Faces marked Up and Down, words or arrows as Greg likes.

SLOT.label: slot
SLOT.notes: "a small slot" (compone.zil 1505); SLOT, adjective SMALL (globals.zil 1357-1363). EXAMINE: "The slot is about ten centimeters wide, but only about two centimeters deep. It is surrounded on its long sides by parallel ridges of metal." (globals.zil 1373-1374; kalamontee.js 105). The fabric's slot: 0.14 wide, horizontal, 1.35 m up, right of the buttons (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1287), bearings 328.2-331.7; the proxy is a little larger, as in Booth 1 and Booth 2. No card works here: every card slid through it gets the wrong-card sign (globals.zil 1382-1431; kalamontee.js 127-155), so the slot's light ("The slot beside the buttons stays dark", connectors.js 243) is dark in every state.

REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR.label: reactor elevator door
REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR.notes: compone.zil 1480-1486, a DOORBIT local global of this room (1513): OPEN and CLOSE get "It won't budge." (1488-1490; connectors.js 262), and its menu offers neither (connectors.js 577). Placed here for the record only: graybox.js draws no plaque for a door (graybox.js 326) and the car's exits are direct (compone.zil 1510-1511), so nothing is registered for it here. Its two metal leaves meet in the middle of the 0.16 m reveal (x -2.18) when shut and slide into the walls either side when open ("The metal doors slide open", globals.zil 2635-2640; fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1273-1279). From in here it is always open (states.DOOR-OPEN): the painting shows the empty doorway.

changes: Painted base, every view: the 2 x 2.5 doorway west open, no leaf in it; in TURN-257, Reactor Control and the Mech Corridor through it as wallOpenings.REACTOR-CONTROL-DOOR's beyond gives them.
DOOR-OPEN.notes: True whenever the player is here, so it is the base and there is no shut variant. The only way in is Reactor Control's EAST or IN, which need the door open (compone.zil 1460-1461); I-REACTOR-DOOR-CLOSE, queued by the button in Reactor Control (globals.zil 2635-2640; connectors.js 521-526), leaves the door alone every turn while HERE is the car and shuts it only after the player has left (compone.zil 1492-1498; connectors.js 430-437); and the door itself will not open or close (compone.zil 1488-1490). The room description says so: "a door to the west, currently open" (compone.zil 1504). The shut leaves are Reactor Control's to paint (its scene alone draws them, fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1273-1279). The review page offers this condition as a switch; it changes nothing in this scene.

changes: Overlay: Floyd's cutout at actors.FLOYD; never painted.
FLOYD-PRESENT.notes: He follows the player in (floyd.js 304-306) or, when he would not otherwise follow, bounces in after him ("Floyd bounces into the elevator", with "Hey, wait for Floyd!", compone.zil 2221-2243; floyd.js 316-320).

constraints: keep the WEST lane and the dropped-item anchors clear
keep off the north wall's panel (bearings 319-333) and the door (244.5-295.5)
FLOYD.notes: The car has no FLOYDBIT (compone.zil 1512), but I-FLOYD names it (compone.zil 2221-2243; floyd.js 316-320). South-east quarter: 0.9 m off the back wall (0.83 m off the handrail), 0.6 m off the south wall, 1.70 m from the eye at bearing 135; his cutout, 0.56 m wide (characters.json FLOYD), spans 125.6-144.4, inside TURN-164 and 7.6 degrees clear of the 071|164 seam window. The car is small: at 1.7 m his feet are below the level views' bottom edge and in the DOWN cap.

droppedItems.notes: Three in the north-east quarter, clear of the panel (its east edge is x -0.9), and two in the south-west, south of the door's line: every anchor 1.15 m or more from the WEST lane (0.5 m required), 0.5 m or more off the walls, and 1.9 m or more from Floyd. Nothing starts here (world.json REACTOR-ELEVATOR objects: none); these take whatever the player drops.

lighting.notes: Proposal for Greg: one old warm-white ceiling fluorescent, as the Upper and Lower Elevators and Booth 2 have (the fabric's lamp at [0, 3.16, 0], fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1336, is only there to see by; its fitting and place are his). The room is ONBIT (compone.zil 1512): lit always, no dark state, no flicker or power state. Beyond the door, Reactor Control lit by its own fixtures. No sky and no day phase. The slot's light is dark in every state.

notes: DR-106 layout (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1069-1071, 1102-1108, 1136, 1280-1290, 1336, 1359; scene wwwroot/data/scenes/REACTOR-ELEVATOR.json, its note at 1435-1438): 4.2 x 3.2 x 3.6, the eye at the middle; one 2 x 2.5 doorway west onto Reactor Control, centred on the car, 0.5 m south of Reactor Control's middle. Canon: "This is an elevator with a door to the west, currently open. A control panel contains an Up button, a Down button, and a small slot." (compone.zil 1503-1505). Flags RLANDBIT ONBIT; globals REACTOR-ELEVATOR-DOOR, SLOT, ELEVATOR-BUTTON, CONTROLS; no scenery words (compone.zil 1512-1513; world.json pseudo []).

Fixed things: the control panel on the north wall by the door -- the Up and Down buttons and the slot, all pick targets (globals above) -- and a handrail along the back (east) wall, 3.2 m long, 0.95 m up (fabric-kalamontee.mjs 1288), bearings 51.7-128.3, in TURN-071 and TURN-164. The handrail is not a game object (no proxy); it stays where the fabric puts it, because Reactor Control's eye sees the car's back wall and the handrail through the open door. One ceiling lamp.

The car never moves (no painted variant for its position): Up and Down give "Nothing happens." Norm plan (DR-106; fabric renders reference/DR-106_REACTOR-ELEVATOR-{071,164,257,350,UP,DOWN}_FABRIC.png): TURN-071/164/257/350 at pitch 0, HFOV 110, 1672x941; caps UP/DOWN at bearing 0, pitch +90/-90, HFOV 133, 1254 square, all from the eye [0, 1.6, 0]. The caps' lens is the one underpaint.mjs caps computes for this ring (lib/views.mjs ringReach, margin 5): the ring reaches 28.95 degrees above and below level at its lowest (bearing 117.5), so each cap needs 2 x (90 - 23.95) = 132.1, rounded up to 133. Spans 93/93/93/81, each under 94. Seam windows (turn.js solveSeams: lo = max(8, span-47), hi = min(span-8, 47)), all on plain wall: 117-118 on the back (east) wall (SE corner 12.6 away; the handrail crosses it, as it crosses every bearing of that wall), 210-211 on the south wall (SW corner 18.4, the door's south jamb 33.5), 303-304 on the west wall north of the door (the door's north jamb 7.5, the NW corner 6.6, the panel 15.3), 24-37 on the north wall (NE corner 12.4, the panel 51.3). The door (244.54-295.46), with everything seen through it, is wholly inside TURN-257, 12.5 degrees left of centre to 38.5 right; the panel (319.3-332.7) inside TURN-350 alone. Corners in frame: TURN-071 the NE (21.6 left of centre), TURN-164 the SE (33.4 left), TURN-257 the SW (27.6 left) and the NW (53.6 right, 1.4 inside the edge), TURN-350 the NW (39.4 left). No view and no cap owns a variant. Seeds first: TURN-257 and TURN-071, 174 degrees apart; TURN-164 and TURN-350 are underpainted from both, then the caps. The panel falls in TURN-350's gap between the seeds (312-16), so it comes from the blockout there and is painted in that view's restore.

The search behind the plan (exhaustive: every ring of 4 or 5 views at 1-degree bearings, at HFOV 100, 110 and 120, scored by the least clearance of any of its seam windows from the four corners, the door's jambs and the panel's edges): no ring does better than 6.6 degrees at any of those lenses or view counts, and 071/164/257/350 is the best 4-view ring at 110, its other windows 12.4 or more clear. (The limit is the whole-degree window, not the geometry: lens 115, outside that search, gets 058/156/254/352, whose window 302.5-303.5 sits in the middle of the north strip, 7.0 clear of the jamb and the corner -- half a degree better; 110 is kept.) What limits it: the clear wall nearest the door is the south wall up to 223.4 (the SW corner less 6) and the north wall from 338.7 (the panel's east edge plus 6; between the NW corner at 310.6 and the panel at 319.3 nothing is clear), 115.3 degrees apart -- more than one view's two seams can span (94 at HFOV 110, 104 at 120; it would take 132). So one of the door view's seams sits on one of the two 15.1-degree strips of west wall beside the door, whose clear middles are 3.1 degrees wide (235.4-238.5 and 301.5-304.6); only the north one works with the other seam on the south wall, and 303-304 is its best window. Not an exception: every window clears every corner, jamb and the panel by 6 or more. One lens, 110, as the admin batch: 120 meets the same 6.6 limit with lopsided spans (103/103/103/51), and 100 needs five views. The eye stays at the middle: the car has no furniture, the door slides (no sweep), and moving the eye east narrows the strips while moving it west widens the door and pushes the panel's clear zone round.

Sky: none. The car is roofed, and everything seen through its door -- Reactor Control and the Mech Corridor's west wall -- is roofed and lit by its own fixtures. No view or cap sees sky, so the room takes no DAY-PHASE and no lighting.sun.

Continuity (ARTWORK-BRIEF 2.6): TURN-257's glimpse must agree with Reactor Control's own paintings, and through its west doorway with the Mech Corridor's. The other way, Reactor Control's open-door variant sees into this car (cast from its eye with the door open): the back wall with the handrail over z -1.8 to 1.5, the east half of the north wall (x 0.1 to 2.1; not the panel), the ceiling and the floor, lit by this car's lamp -- they must agree with TURN-071 and the right of TURN-350. Whichever room is accepted first is the reference for the other.
